subproblem.title: Area formula, multiplicity and weighted forms (Simon 2.3.4, 2.3.5, erratum dHⁿ)
subproblem.statement: For n ≤ m, A ⊆ ℝⁿ Lebesgue-null-measurable and f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ K-Lipschitz on A, with Jf(x) = √det(L*L), L = fderivWithin ℝ f A x: (3.4, corrected) ∫_{ℝᵐ} #(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_A Jf dLⁿ; (3.5) for every h : ℝⁿ → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable on A, y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ A ∩ f⁻¹{y}} h(x) is Hⁿ-a.e.-measurable and its Hⁿ-integral equals ∫_A h Jf dLⁿ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §3, 3.1-3.5 and the printed arguments (pp. 53-54). Erratum applied (GMT/Ch02/README.md and the SimonGMT ledger): in 3.4 the printed target measure dH^m(y) is corrected to dH^n(y) (as printed in 3.5); with H^m, m > n, the left side would be 0 or ∞. The printed text proves only the linear case 3.1 and refers to [Har79]/[Fed69] for 3.2; the general nonlinear statement is available as kernel-checked theorems of the pinned SimonGMT library (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/AreaDomain.lean, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only), so the remaining work is to identify the frozen notions with the library ones.

PART I. PRINTED ARGUMENT (cleaned transcription).
3.1. If L is a linear map ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k}, k ≥ 0, then L(ℝⁿ) ⊆ F with F an n-dimensional subspace; choosing an orthogonal q with q(F) = ℝⁿ × {0} and p(x,y) = x, p∘q∘L : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ and Lⁿ((p∘q∘L)(A)) = |det(p∘q∘L)|Lⁿ(A); since (p∘q∘L)*(p∘q∘L) = L*∘q*∘(p*∘p)∘q∘L = L*∘L, |det(p∘q∘L)| = √det(L*∘L), and since q is an isometry, H^n(L(A)) = √det(L*∘L) H^n(A), A ⊆ ℝⁿ.
3.2. More generally, given a 1:1 Lipschitz f : A → ℝ^m (A ⊆ ℝⁿ Lebesgue measurable, m ≥ n), by an approximation argument based on the linear case 3.1 (see [Har79] or [Fed69]), H^n(f(A)) = ∫_A Jf dH^n, where Jf(y) = √det(df_y* ∘ df_y) (3.3).
3.4. If f is not 1:1 we have the general area formula (which follows quite easily from 3.2) ∫_{ℝ^m} H⁰(f⁻¹(y) ∩ A) dH^n(y) = ∫_A Jf dLⁿ [erratum: dH^n, not dH^m], where H⁰(f⁻¹(y) ∩ A) is the multiplicity N(f,y).
3.5. More generally, if h is a non-negative H^n-measurable function on A, then ∫ Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(y)} h(x) dH^n(y) = ∫_A h Jf dH^n. This follows directly from 3.4 if we approximate h by simple functions.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF THE FROZEN STATEMENT AreaFormula.
Let n ≤ m, A ⊆ ℝⁿ with NullMeasurableSet A volume, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ with LipschitzOnWith K f A (ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)). Write L_x := fderivWithin ℝ f A x : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝᵐ.

1. Library theorems used (namespace Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02, with E = ℝⁿ, F = ℝᵐ, s = A, any K):
 (a) weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum (hs : NullMeasurableSet s volume) (hL : LipschitzOnWith K f s) (hw : AEMeasurable w (volume.restrict s)) : ∫⁻ y, weightedAreaFiberSum s f w y ∂μHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal (areaJacobianWithin f s x) * w x ∂volume;
 (b) aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn (same hypotheses) : AEMeasurable (weightedAreaFiberSum s f w) μHE[finrank ℝ E];
 (c) area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity (hs) (hL) : ∫⁻ y, areaMultiplicity s f y ∂μHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal (areaJacobianWithin f s x) ∂volume.
 Mathematically these are 3.2-3.5: the library proves them by extending f to a global Lipschitz map (componentwise McShane extension), Rademacher, the approximation of the Lipschitz map on countably many Borel pieces by linear maps (Federer's argument) with the linear case 3.1, and the identification of fderivWithin with the derivative of the extension at a.e. point of A (density points).
2. Dimension: finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) = n (Mathlib finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so μHE[finrank ℝ ℝⁿ] = μHE[n] after rewriting.
3. Jacobian: areaJacobianWithin f A x = (L_x).normDet (definition, via the underlying linear map). For any linear map L between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, normDet L ≥ 0 and (normDet L)² = det(L* ∘ L) (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_nonneg, LinearMap.normDet_sq; also SimonGMT areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp), hence normDet L = √det(L*∘L). The continuous-linear determinant of ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L_x ∘L L_x equals the linear determinant of the corresponding linear map, so areaJacobian (fderivWithin ℝ f A x) = Real.sqrt((ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L_x ∘L L_x).det) = areaJacobianWithin f A x for every x.
4. Fibers: areaFiber A f y = {x // x ∈ A ∧ f x = y}, while ↥(A ∩ f⁻¹'{y}) = {x // x ∈ A ∩ f⁻¹'{y}}; membership x ∈ A ∩ f⁻¹'{y} unfolds definitionally to x ∈ A ∧ f x = y. Hence weightedAreaFiberSum A f h y = ∑' x : areaFiber A f y, h x.1 = ∑' x : ↥(A ∩ f⁻¹'{y}), h x (equal index types, or transport along the obvious equivalence of subtypes, Equiv.tsum_eq). Likewise areaMultiplicity A f y = ∑' _ : ↥(A ∩ f⁻¹'{y}), 1 = ENat.toENNReal (A ∩ f⁻¹'{y}).encard (Mathlib ENNReal.tsum_set_one) = fiberCount A f y.
5. (3.4) By 1(c), 2, 3, 4: ∫⁻ y, fiberCount A f y ∂μHE[n] = ∫⁻ x in A, ENNReal.ofReal (areaJacobian (fderivWithin ℝ f A x)) ∂volume. This is the first conjunct (the corrected 3.4).
6. (3.5) Let h : ℝⁿ → [0,∞] be AEMeasurable for volume restricted to A. By 1(b), 2, 4 the function y ↦ ∑' x : ↥(A ∩ f⁻¹'{y}), h x is AEMeasurable for μHE[n]; by 1(a), 2, 3, 4 its μHE[n]-integral equals ∫⁻ x in A, ENNReal.ofReal(areaJacobian(fderivWithin ℝ f A x)) * h x ∂volume = ∫⁻ x in A, h x * ENNReal.ofReal(areaJacobian(fderivWithin ℝ f A x)) ∂volume (commutativity of multiplication in ENNReal). This is the second conjunct (3.5; here Hⁿ on the source ℝⁿ is volume, as recorded in the contract).
7. The hypothesis n ≤ m is not needed by the library statements (it only reflects the printed setting). Steps 5 and 6 prove AreaFormula.
proof_key_steps: Printed route: linear case 3.1, approximation for injective Lipschitz maps 3.2, multiplicity 3.4, simple-function approximation 3.5.
Invoke the kernel-checked SimonGMT theorems weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn and area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity.
Identify finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n, areaJacobianWithin = normDet = √det(L*L) = areaJacobian, weightedAreaFiberSum = tsum over A ∩ f⁻¹{y}, areaMultiplicity = encard = fiberCount, and commute the product.

subproblem.title: BV compactness (Simon 2.2.6), BV Poincaré inequality (2.2.7) and BV extension estimate (2.2.8)
subproblem.statement: (2.6) If U ⊆ ℝⁿ and u_k (k ∈ ℕ) are locally BV on U (SimonGMT IsLocallyBV) and, for every open W ⊂⊂ U, sup_k ∫_W (|u_k(x)| + |Du_k|(W)) dLⁿ(x) < ∞, where |Du|(W) = SimonGMT bvVariationOn u W is an x-independent constant inside the integrand (so the hypothesis is sup_k (∫_W|u_k| + Lⁿ(W)·|Du_k|(W)) < ∞; Lean: ⨆ k, (∫⁻ x in W, ‖u k x‖ₑ + bvVariationOn (u k) W) < ⊤), then a subsequence u_{ψ(k)} (ψ strictly increasing) converges in L¹_loc(U) to a locally BV v with |Dv|(W) ≤ liminf |Du_{ψ(k)}|(W) for all open W ⊂⊂ U. (2.7) For all n and θ, δ ∈ (0,1) there is C ≥ 0 such that for bounded open convex U, R > 0, ξ ∈ U with B̄(ξ,δR) ⊆ U ⊆ B̄(ξ,R), u ∈ BV(U) (u ∈ L¹(U), |Du|(U) < ∞) and β with θLⁿ(U) ≤ min(Lⁿ{u ≥ β}, Lⁿ{u ≤ β}) (sets inside U): ∫_U|u − β| ≤ C R |Du|(U). (2.8) For all n and δ ∈ (0,1) there is C ≥ 0 such that for U, R, ξ as in 2.7 and u ∈ BV(ℝⁿ) with u = 0 a.e. off Ū: |Du|(ℝⁿ∖Ū) = 0 and |Du|(ℝⁿ) ≤ C(|Du|(U) + R⁻¹∫_U|u|).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §2: Lemma 2.5, Theorem 2.6, Lemma 2.7, Lemma 2.8 with their printed proofs (pp. 48-53). Errata/readings applied (GMT/Ch02/README.md): in 2.6 the sets W ⊂⊂ U are taken open (lower semicontinuity fails for non-open W; 2.4 characterizes |Du|(W) only for open W); in 2.7, u ∈ BV(U) includes u ∈ L¹(U); in 2.8, spt u ⊂ Ū means u = 0 a.e. off Ū and ∫_{ℝⁿ}|Du| = ∫_Ū|Du| is encoded as |Du|(ℝⁿ∖Ū) = 0. Frozen form of the 2.6 hypothesis (Contract.lean, BVCompactness): it reads ⨆ k, (∫⁻ x in W, ‖u k x‖ₑ + Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W) < ⊤ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, where the whole sum ‖u k x‖ₑ + bvVariationOn (u k) W is the integrand; that is, sup_k ∫_W (|u_k(x)| + |Du_k|(W)) dLⁿ(x) < ∞ with the x-independent constant |Du_k|(W) inside the integral, which equals sup_k (∫_W |u_k| + Lⁿ(W)·|Du_k|(W)) < ∞. Step A0 below derives from it the printed (unweighted) bound sup_k (∫_W |u_k| + |Du_k|(W)) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and only this derived finite constant is used in A1 and A4. The printed proofs cite [GT01, Thm 7.22] (compactness) and the smooth Poincaré inequality [GT01]; complete arguments are supplied. For 2.8 the printed cut-off argument is kept but the final passage to the limit is done directly on test fields (no product lower-semicontinuity is needed).

Notation (frozen definitions, SimonGMT Chapter02/BV.lean). ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Lⁿ = volume. For a vector field g, div g := trace(fderiv g) (Rademacher a.e. derivative for Lipschitz g). An admissible field for an open set W is a compactly supported Lipschitz g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with tsupport g ⊆ W and sup|g| ≤ 1. |Du|(W) := bvVariationOn u W = sup over admissible g of ofReal(∫_W u div g) ∈ [0,∞]. Since g and −g are both admissible, |∫_W u div g| ≤ (sup|g|)|Du|(W) for every compactly supported Lipschitz g with tsupport g ⊆ W. W ⊆ W′ open ⇒ |Du|(W) ≤ |Du|(W′). IsLocallyBV U u: U open, u ∈ L¹_loc(U), and for each open W ⊂⊂ U a constant c(W) with ∫_W u div g ≤ c(W) sup|g| for C¹ compactly supported g, tsupport g ⊆ W. W ⊂⊂ U: closure W compact and ⊆ U. TendstoLocallyInL1On v u U: ∫_Q |v_i − u| → 0 for every compact Q ⊆ U. IsBVOn U u: U open, u ∈ L¹(U), |Du|(U) < ∞. For an open W and σ > 0 put W^(σ) := {x : dist(x, ℝⁿ∖W) > σ}, an open set, where dist(x, ∅) := +∞ (i.e. use the extended distance infEdist, so W^(σ) = ℝⁿ when W = ℝⁿ). Every point within distance ≤ σ of W^(σ) lies in W.

PART I. PRINTED PROOFS (cleaned transcription).
Lemma 2.5. If u ∈ BV_loc(U) then u_(σ) → u in L¹_loc(U) and |Du_(σ)| → |Du| as Radon measures. (Printed proof: convergence in L¹_loc is standard; (2) ∫ f|Du| ≤ liminf ∫ f|Du_(σ)| by definition of |Du|; for (3) note (4) ∫ f|Du_(σ)| = sup_{|g|≤f, g smooth} ∫ g·∇u_(σ), and for fixed smooth g with |g| ≤ f and σ < dist(spt f, ∂U): ∫ g·∇u_(σ) = −∫ u_(σ) div g = −∫ φ_σ * u div g = −∫ u φ_σ * div g = −∫ u div(φ_σ * g) ≤ ∫_{W_σ}(f + ε(σ))|Du| since |φ_σ * g| ≤ φ_σ * |g| ≤ φ_σ * f and φ_σ * f → f uniformly.)
Theorem 2.6 (printed proof). By virtue of the previous lemma, in order to prove u_{k′} → u in L¹_loc(U) for some subsequence, it is enough to prove that the sets {u ∈ C¹(U) : ∫_W (|u| + |Du|) dLⁿ ≤ c(W)}, W ⊂⊂ U (for given constants c(W) < ∞), are precompact in L¹_loc(U). For the simple proof of this (involving mollification and Arzela's theorem) see [GT01, Thm 7.22]. Finally the fact that ∫_W|Du| ≤ liminf ∫_W |Du_{k′}| is a direct consequence of the definition of |Du|, |Du_{k′}|.
Lemma 2.7 (printed proof). By rescaling x ↦ R⁻¹(x − ξ) we can assume R = 1, ξ = 0. Let β, θ be as in 2.7(*) and choose convex W ⊂⊂ U such that (*) ∫_W |u − β| ≥ ½∫_U |u − β| and such that 2.7(*) holds with W in place of U and θ/2 in place of θ (e.g. W = {x ∈ U : dist(x, ∂U) > σ} with σ small). Letting u_σ denote the mollified functions, for sufficiently small σ we have 2.7(*) with u_σ in place of u, θ/4 in place of θ and W in place of U. Hence by the usual Poincaré inequality for smooth functions we have, with suitable β(σ) → β, ∫_W |u_σ − β(σ)| ≤ c ∫_W |Du_σ|, c = c(n,θ,δ), for all sufficiently small σ. The required inequality follows by letting σ ↓ 0 and using (*) and 2.5.
Lemma 2.8 (printed proof). Assume R = 1, ξ = 0. Let d(x) = dist(x, ∂U). Since U is convex, U_σ = {x : dist(x,∂U) > σ} is convex for each σ ≥ 0 […] and 0 < d(x) < d(y) ⇒ (y − x)·Dd(x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ U at which d is differentiable. Since B_δ(0) ⊆ U and |Dd(x)| = 1 at points of differentiability in U, taking y = −δDd(x) gives (1) x·Dd(x) ≤ −δ for a.e. x ∈ U with d(x) < dist(B_δ(0), ∂U). Let γ : ℝ → [0,1] be increasing, C¹, γ(t) = 0 for t ≤ σ/2, γ(t) = 1 for t ≥ σ, and (2) φ = γ∘d. Then (3) δ|Dφ(x)| ≤ −x·Dφ(x). By definition of |Dw|, (4) ∫|D(φu)| ≤ ∫|Dφ||u| + ∫ φ|Du|, and by (3) (5) δ∫|Dφ||u| ≤ −∫ x·Dφ |u| = ∫ |u| div(xφ) … ≤ ∫_U |D|u|| + n∫|u| ≤ ∫_U |Du| + n∫|u| (because |D|u|| ≤ |Du| by 2.5 and lower semicontinuity). Finally ∫_{ℝⁿ}|Du| ≤ liminf ∫|D(φu)| since φu → u in L¹, and 2.8 follows from (4), (5).

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF BVCompactness ∧ BVPoincare ∧ BVExtensionEstimate.

Section T (common tools).
T1 (mollifiers). Fix φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ), φ ≥ 0, spt φ ⊆ B(0,1), ∫φ = 1, φ(−x) = φ(x); φ_σ(x) := σ^{−n}φ(x/σ). For F ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), F_σ := φ_σ * F is C^∞ (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), ∂_i F_σ = (∂_iφ_σ) * F, sup|F_σ| ≤ sup|φ_σ|·‖F‖₁ and Lip(F_σ) ≤ sup|Dφ_σ|·‖F‖₁.
T2 (L¹ convergence). For F ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), ‖F_σ − F‖₁ → 0 as σ → 0. Proof: given ε choose F₀ continuous with compact support and ‖F − F₀‖₁ < ε (density of C_c in L¹); ‖φ_σ*(F − F₀)‖₁ ≤ ‖F − F₀‖₁ (Young/Tonelli, ∫φ_σ = 1); φ_σ*F₀ → F₀ uniformly (uniform continuity) with supports in a fixed compact set, hence in L¹. So limsup ‖F_σ − F‖₁ ≤ 2ε.
T3 (integration by parts for Lipschitz functions). If F : ℝⁿ → ℝ is Lipschitz and g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ is Lipschitz with compact support then ∫ F div g = −∫ ∇F·g (a.e. derivatives). This is the Fubini/absolute-continuity-on-lines argument of the printed proof of Rademacher; formally Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq applied to f := F, the coordinate functions g_i = ⟨e_i, g⟩ and v := e_i, together with lineDeriv_neg and the a.e. identities lineDeriv = fderiv at differentiability points (Rademacher) and div g = Σ_i⟨e_i, Dg e_i⟩ (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence_eq_sum_inner). (If F is only Lipschitz on a neighbourhood N of tsupport g, apply this to χF with χ ∈ C_c^∞(N) equal to 1 near tsupport g.)
T4 (variation of a mollification). Let W be open, u ∈ L¹(W), F := u·1_W, σ > 0 and g a C^∞ (or C¹) compactly supported field with tsupport g ⊆ W^(σ) and sup|g| ≤ 1. Then ∫ F_σ div g = ∫ F (φ_σ * div g) = ∫_W u div(φ_σ * g) ≤ |Du|(W). Indeed Fubini and φ_σ(−x) = φ_σ(x) give the first equality; φ_σ * div g = div(φ_σ * g); and φ_σ * g is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ tsupport g + B̄(0,σ) ⊆ W and sup|φ_σ * g| ≤ 1, hence admissible for W.
T5 (smooth duality). For w ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) and O open, ∫_O |∇w| ≤ sup{∫ w div g : g ∈ C_c^∞(O; ℝⁿ), |g| ≤ 1}. Proof: take compact K_l ↑ O, χ_l ∈ C_c^∞(O) with 0 ≤ χ_l ≤ 1, χ_l = 1 on K_l, and g := −χ_l ∇w/√(|∇w|² + η²) (C^∞, |g| ≤ 1). Then ∫ w div g = −∫ ∇w·g (smooth integration by parts) = ∫ χ_l |∇w|²/√(|∇w|²+η²) ≥ ∫_{K_l} (|∇w| − η) (as t²/√(t²+η²) ≥ t − η for t ≥ 0); let η → 0 and l → ∞ (monotone convergence).
T6 (gradient bound). Combining T4 and T5 (with O = W^(σ)): for u ∈ L¹(W), ∫_{W^(σ)} |∇(φ_σ*(u1_W))| ≤ |Du|(W).
T7 (translation and mollification estimate). Let W open, u ∈ L¹(W), Q compact, σ > 0 with Q + B̄(0,3σ) ⊆ W, and u_σ := φ_σ * (u1_W). Then for |z| ≤ σ: ∫_Q |u(x − z) − u(x)| dx ≤ |z| |Du|(W), and ∫_Q |u_σ − u| ≤ σ|Du|(W). Proof: for 0 < τ < σ let w := φ_τ * (u1_W) (smooth). For x ∈ Q, |w(x−z) − w(x)| ≤ |z|∫_0^1 |∇w(x − tz)| dt; integrating over Q and using Tonelli and translation invariance, ∫_Q |w(x−z) − w(x)| dx ≤ |z| ∫_{Q+B̄(0,σ)} |∇w| ≤ |z| ∫_{W^(τ)} |∇w| ≤ |z||Du|(W) (Q + B̄(0,σ) ⊆ W^(τ) because points of Q + B̄(0,σ) have distance > 2σ > τ from ℝⁿ∖W; then T6). As τ → 0, w → u1_W in L¹(ℝⁿ) (T2), and x, x − z ∈ W for x ∈ Q, so the left side converges to ∫_Q |u(x−z) − u(x)| dx. Finally, for x ∈ Q, u_σ(x) − u(x) = ∫ φ_σ(z)(u(x−z) − u(x)) dz, so by Tonelli ∫_Q |u_σ − u| ≤ ∫ φ_σ(z) ∫_Q |u(x−z) − u(x)| dx dz ≤ σ|Du|(W).
T8 (|D|u|| ≤ |Du|). For O open and u ∈ L¹_loc(O): |D|u||(O) ≤ |Du|(O). Proof: let g be admissible for O, and choose open sets W ⊂⊂ W′ ⊂⊂ O with tsupport g ⊆ W, and σ_j ↓ 0 with W ⊆ W′^(σ_j). Let w_j := φ_{σ_j} * (u1_{W′}) and ψ_η(t) := √(t² + η²) − η (smooth, |ψ_η′| ≤ 1, |ψ_η(t) − |t|| ≤ η). The function ψ_η∘w_j is globally Lipschitz (Lip ≤ Lip w_j ≤ sup|Dφ_{σ_j}|·‖u1_{W′}‖₁ by T1), so by T3 and T6, ∫ ψ_{η}(w_j) div g = −∫ ψ_η′(w_j)∇w_j·g ≤ ∫_W |∇w_j| ≤ |Du|(W′) ≤ |Du|(O). Taking η = η_j → 0, ψ_{η_j}(w_j) → |u| in L¹(W) (T2 and the two bounds on ψ_η), and div g is bounded, so ∫_O |u| div g = ∫_W |u| div g ≤ |Du|(O). Taking the supremum over g gives the claim.

Section A (Theorem 2.6, BVCompactness). Hypotheses (exact frozen form): every u_k satisfies IsLocallyBV U (so U is open, by the case k = 0, and u_k ∈ L¹_loc(U)), and for every open W ⊂⊂ U: S_W := sup_k ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) dLⁿ(x) < ∞, where |Du_k|(W) := bvVariationOn (u k) W ∈ [0,∞] does not depend on x (it is a constant inside the integrand).
A0. Unweighted uniform bound. Claim: for every open W ⊂⊂ U the quantity C_W := sup_k (∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) ∈ [0,∞] is finite.
(a) W = ∅. The integral over ∅ is 0 (the restricted measure is the zero measure), and |Du_k|(∅) = 0: every term of the supremum defining bvVariationOn (u k) ∅ is ofReal(∫_∅ u_k div g) = ofReal 0 = 0, and a supremum of zeros (also an empty one) is 0 in [0,∞]. Hence both terms vanish for every k and C_∅ = 0.
(b) W ≠ ∅. Then 0 < Lⁿ(W) < ∞: W is a nonempty open set and Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets (Mathlib IsOpen.measure_pos; this also holds for n = 0, where ℝ⁰ is a point of measure 1); and Lⁿ(W) ≤ Lⁿ(closure W) < ∞ because closure W is compact (Mathlib IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Fix k. Since x ↦ |Du_k|(W) is constant, hence measurable, the integral splits (Mathlib lintegral_add_right with measurable_const, then setLIntegral_const): ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) dx = ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)·Lⁿ(W). This is ≤ S_W, so ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ S_W and |Du_k|(W)·Lⁿ(W) ≤ S_W; dividing by Lⁿ(W) ∈ (0,∞) gives |Du_k|(W) ≤ S_W/Lⁿ(W) (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, using Lⁿ(W) ≠ 0 and Lⁿ(W) ≠ ∞). Therefore ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W) ≤ S_W + S_W/Lⁿ(W) for every k, and C_W ≤ S_W + S_W/Lⁿ(W) < ∞ because S_W < ∞ and Lⁿ(W) ≠ 0 (ENNReal.div_lt_top).
(c) Consequences used below. For every open W ⊂⊂ U put c_W := C_W.toReal ∈ [0,∞) (finite by (a), (b)). Then for every k: u_k is integrable on W (u_k ∈ L¹_loc(U) and closure W is a compact subset of U) with ∫_W |u_k| ≤ c_W; |Du_k|(W) ≤ C_W < ∞, so |Du_k|(W).toReal ≤ c_W. In words: sup_k (∫_W |u_k| + |Du_k|(W)) ≤ c_W < ∞, the printed hypothesis of 2.6.
A1. Total boundedness on compacts. Fix compact Q ⊆ U (if Q = ∅ there is nothing to prove). Choose δ > 0 with Q + B̄(0,2δ) ⊆ U (Q compact, U open), the open set W := {x : dist(x,Q) < δ} (so Q ⊆ W, and closure W ⊆ Q + B̄(0,δ) is compact and contained in U, i.e. W ⊂⊂ U) and σ₀ := δ/4 (so Q + B̄(0,3σ₀) ⊆ W). Let c_W ∈ [0,∞) be the finite constant of A0 for this W. Given ε > 0 choose σ ∈ (0, σ₀] with σc_W < ε/4. By T7 (applied to u_k ∈ L¹(W), with |Du_k|(W) ≤ c_W by A0(c)), ∫_Q |(u_k)_σ − u_k| ≤ σc_W < ε/4 for all k, where (u_k)_σ := φ_σ*(u_k1_W). By T1 and ‖u_k1_W‖₁ = ∫_W |u_k| ≤ c_W (A0(c)), the restrictions (u_k)_σ|_Q are bounded by B := sup|φ_σ|·c_W and Λ-Lipschitz with Λ := sup|Dφ_σ|·c_W. Elementary Arzelà-Ascoli: with η := ε/(4(Lⁿ(Q) + 1)), pick a finite η/(3Λ+1)-net q_1,…,q_p of Q and the finite grid of multiples of η/3 in [−B,B]; two functions whose rounded values at all q_i coincide differ by at most η everywhere on Q; so finitely many indices k_1,…,k_r exist such that every (u_k)_σ is within η in sup norm, hence within ε/4 in L¹(Q), of some (u_{k_s})_σ. Consequently every u_k is within ε/4 + ε/4 + ε/4 < ε in L¹(Q) of some u_{k_s}: {u_k|_Q} is totally bounded in L¹(Q).
A2. Diagonal extraction. Let Q_1 ⊆ Q_2 ⊆ … be compact with Q_j ⊆ interior Q_{j+1} and ∪Q_j = U. By A1 and the pigeonhole principle, from any subsequence one can extract a further subsequence that is Cauchy in L¹(Q_j); doing this successively for j = 1, 2, … and taking the diagonal gives a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ such that (u_{ψ(k)}) is Cauchy in L¹(Q_j) for every j. By completeness of L¹(Q_j) let v_j be its limit; v_{j+1} = v_j a.e. on Q_j. Define v := v_j on Q_j∖Q_{j−1} (measurable representatives) and v := 0 off U. Then ∫_{Q_j} |u_{ψ(k)} − v| → 0 for every j. Every compact K ⊆ U is contained in some Q_j (it is covered by the increasing open sets interior Q_{j+1}), so TendstoLocallyInL1On (u∘ψ) v U holds; and v ∈ L¹_loc(U) since ∫_K |v| ≤ ∫_K |v − u_{ψ(k)}| + ∫_K |u_{ψ(k)}| < ∞.
A3. Lower semicontinuity: for open W ⊂⊂ U, |Dv|(W) ≤ liminf_k |Du_{ψ(k)}|(W). This is SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.bvVariationOn_le_liminf_of_locallyL1 (for each admissible g, ∫_W v div g = lim_k ∫_W u_{ψ(k)} div g because u_{ψ(k)} → v in L¹(closure W) and div g is bounded; and each term is ≤ |Du_{ψ(k)}|(W)).
A4. v is locally BV. Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U and c_W ≥ 0 the constant of A0. Claim: for every k and every C¹ compactly supported field g (IsC1TestField g) with tsupport g ⊆ W, ∫_W u_k div g ≤ c_W·sup|g|, where sup|g| := compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≥ 0. Put s := sup|g|. If s = 0 then g ≡ 0, so div g ≡ 0 and ∫_W u_k div g = 0 = c_W·s. If s > 0 then h := s⁻¹g is a Lipschitz test field (a compactly supported C¹ field is Lipschitz, SimonGMT IsC1TestField.isLipschitzTestField, and scaling preserves this) with tsupport h = tsupport g ⊆ W and sup|h| = 1 ≤ 1; since g is differentiable, fderiv h = s⁻¹ fderiv g, so div h = s⁻¹ div g and ∫_W u_k div h = s⁻¹∫_W u_k div g. By SimonGMT ofReal_integral_le_bvVariationOn, ofReal(s⁻¹∫_W u_k div g) ≤ |Du_k|(W) < ∞, hence s⁻¹∫_W u_k div g ≤ |Du_k|(W).toReal ≤ c_W (A0(c)), i.e. ∫_W u_k div g ≤ c_W·s. Thus the hypothesis hbound of SimonGMT isLocallyBV_of_locallyL1_of_uniform_bound holds with the constant c := c_W ≥ 0 for all indices (in particular eventually along atTop for the subsequence u_{ψ(k)}); together with U open, v ∈ L¹_loc(U), u_{ψ(k)} ∈ L¹_loc(U) and TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop from A2, that lemma gives IsLocallyBV U v. (Mathematically: ∫_W v div g = lim_k ∫_W u_{ψ(k)} div g ≤ c_W sup|g|, because u_{ψ(k)} → v in L¹(closure W) and div g is bounded.)
A5. A2-A4 give ψ, v with StrictMono ψ, IsLocallyBV U v, TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop and the liminf inequality for all open W ⊂⊂ U: BVCompactness. (If U = ∅ everything is trivial.)

Section B (Lemma 2.7, BVPoincare). Given n and θ, δ ∈ (0,1) put C := 2^{n+1}(1 + θ⁻¹) (it does not even depend on δ). Let U, R, ξ, u, β be as in the statement; in particular u ∈ L¹(U), |Du|(U) < ∞, ξ ∈ U, B̄(ξ,δR) ⊆ U ⊆ B̄(ξ,R), so 0 < Lⁿ(U) < ∞ and diam U ≤ 2R. (n = 0: U is the single point of ℝ⁰ and the hypothesis on β forces u = β there, so both sides vanish; the general argument below also covers it.)
B1. Smooth Poincaré on convex sets. If O is open, convex, bounded with Lⁿ(O) > 0 and w ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ), then ∫_O∫_O |w(x) − w(y)| dx dy ≤ 2ⁿ diam(O) Lⁿ(O) ∫_O |∇w|, hence ∫_O |w − w̄_O| ≤ 2ⁿ diam(O) ∫_O |∇w| where w̄_O is the mean of w on O. Proof: |w(x) − w(y)| ≤ |y − x| ∫_0^1 |∇w(x + t(y − x))| dt (the segment lies in O). For t ∈ [½,1] and fixed x substitute z = (1−t)x + ty: dy = t^{−n} dz ≤ 2ⁿ dz and z ∈ O; for t ∈ [0,½] and fixed y substitute z = (1−t)x + ty: dx = (1−t)^{−n} dz ≤ 2ⁿ dz. Each half contributes at most ½·diam(O)·Lⁿ(O)·2ⁿ∫_O|∇w|. Then ∫_O |w(x) − w̄_O| dx ≤ Lⁿ(O)⁻¹ ∫_O∫_O |w(x) − w(y)| dy dx.
From here on in Section B assume n ≥ 1 (so U, being bounded, is not all of ℝⁿ and d below is finite and positive exactly on U).
B2. Inner parallel sets. d(x) := dist(x, ℝⁿ∖U) is concave on U (if B(x,a) ⊆ U and B(y,b) ⊆ U then B((1−t)x+ty, (1−t)a+tb) ⊆ U by convexity), so U_σ := U^(σ) = {d > σ} is open, convex, bounded, U_σ ↑ U as σ ↓ 0, and ξ ∈ U_σ, Lⁿ(U_σ) > 0 for small σ.
B3. Approximation. Let w_σ := φ_σ*(u1_U) (C^∞). By T6, ∫_{U_σ} |∇w_σ| ≤ |Du|(U). By B1, ∫_{U_σ} |w_σ − c_σ| ≤ 2ⁿ·2R·|Du|(U), c_σ := mean of w_σ on U_σ.
B4. Limit σ → 0. By T2, ‖w_σ − u1_U‖_{L¹(ℝⁿ)} → 0; Lⁿ(U∖U_σ) → 0 and ∫_{U∖U_σ}|u| → 0. Hence ∫_{U_σ} w_σ → ∫_U u and Lⁿ(U_σ) → Lⁿ(U), so c_σ → ū := mean of u on U; and |∫_{U_σ}|w_σ − c_σ| − ∫_U |u − ū|| ≤ ‖w_σ − u1_U‖₁ + |c_σ − ū|Lⁿ(U) + ∫_{U∖U_σ}|u − ū| → 0. Therefore ∫_U |u − ū| ≤ 2^{n+1}R |Du|(U).
B5. From the mean to β. (The sets {x ∈ U : u ≥ β} and {x ∈ U : u ≤ β} are null-measurable since u is a.e.-measurable on the measurable set U, so their measures can be used in lower bounds for integrals, e.g. Mathlib mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀.) If β ≥ ū then |u − ū| ≥ β − ū on {x ∈ U : u ≥ β}, a set of measure ≥ θLⁿ(U); if β < ū then |u − ū| ≥ ū − β on {x ∈ U : u ≤ β}, also of measure ≥ θLⁿ(U). In both cases θLⁿ(U)|β − ū| ≤ ∫_U |u − ū|. Hence ∫_U |u − β| ≤ ∫_U |u − ū| + Lⁿ(U)|ū − β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)∫_U|u − ū| ≤ C R |Du|(U). In the frozen form: ∫⁻ x in U, ‖u x − β‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(C·R)·bvVariationOn u U (both sides finite; C ≥ 0).

Section C (Lemma 2.8, BVExtensionEstimate). Given n and δ ∈ (0,1) put C := max(1 + δ⁻¹, nδ⁻¹) ≥ 0. Let U, R, ξ be as in the statement, u ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) with |Du|(ℝⁿ) < ∞ (IsBVOn univ u) and u = 0 a.e. on ℝⁿ∖Ū. (n = 0: ℝ⁰ = U = Ū, (Ū)ᶜ = ∅ and both claims are trivial since C ≥ 1; assume n ≥ 1, so U ≠ ℝⁿ as U is bounded.)
C0. |Du|(ℝⁿ∖Ū) = 0: for g admissible for the open set ℝⁿ∖Ū, ∫_{ℝⁿ∖Ū} u div g = 0 because u = 0 a.e. there; so every term of the supremum is ofReal 0 = 0.
C1. d(x) := dist(x, ℝⁿ∖U) is 1-Lipschitz, zero off U, concave on U (B2), and |∇d(x)| = 1 at every x ∈ U where d is differentiable: |∇d| ≤ 1 by the Lipschitz bound, and if a ∉ U is a nearest point to x and e := (a − x)/|a − x| then d(x + se) ≤ d(x) − s for 0 ≤ s ≤ d(x), so ∇d(x)·e ≤ −1.
C2. Let η₀ := dist(B̄(ξ,δR), ℝⁿ∖U) > 0 (compact subset of the open U). For x ∈ U with d differentiable at x and d(x) < η₀: −(x − ξ)·∇d(x) ≥ δR. Proof: w := ξ − δR∇d(x) ∈ B̄(ξ,δR) ⊆ U, so d(w) ≥ η₀ > d(x); concavity on the segment [x,w] ⊆ U gives the supergradient inequality d(w) ≤ d(x) + ∇d(x)·(w − x); hence ∇d(x)·(ξ − x) − δR|∇d(x)|² > 0 with |∇d(x)| = 1.
C3. Cut-offs. The level sets {d = c}, c > 0, are disjoint subsets of U (finite measure), so only countably many have positive measure; choose ε_j ↓ 0 with ε_j < η₀ and Lⁿ({d = ε_j}) = Lⁿ({d = ε_j/2}) = 0. Let γ_ε(t) := min{1, max{0, 2t/ε − 1}} and φ_ε := γ_ε∘d: Lipschitz, 0 ≤ φ_ε ≤ 1, φ_ε = 0 on {d ≤ ε/2}, so tsupport φ_ε ⊆ {d ≥ ε/2}, a compact subset of U (closed and bounded); φ_ε = 1 on {d ≥ ε}; φ_ε → 1_U pointwise as ε → 0. For a.e. x: ∇φ_ε(x) = (2/ε)∇d(x) if ε/2 < d(x) < ε and ∇φ_ε(x) = 0 if d(x) < ε/2 or d(x) > ε (open sets on which φ_ε is an affine function of d, resp. constant), the two level sets being null for ε = ε_j. By C2, for a.e. x: δR|∇φ_ε(x)| ≤ −(x − ξ)·∇φ_ε(x).
C4. Key bound: ∫ |u||∇φ_ε| ≤ δ⁻¹|Du|(U) + nδ⁻¹R⁻¹∫_U |u|. Let V(x) := (x − ξ)φ_ε(x)/R: Lipschitz, tsupport V ⊆ tsupport φ_ε ⊆ U compact, |V| ≤ 1 (|x − ξ| ≤ R on U), and div V = (nφ_ε + (x − ξ)·∇φ_ε)/R a.e. Then ∫|u||∇φ_ε| ≤ (δR)⁻¹ ∫ |u|(−(x − ξ)·∇φ_ε) = (δR)⁻¹ (n∫|u|φ_ε − R∫_U |u| div V) ≤ (δR)⁻¹(n∫_U|u| + R|D|u||(U)), and |D|u||(U) ≤ |Du|(U) by T8.
C5. Bound on |Du|(ℝⁿ). Let g be admissible for ℝⁿ. Since u ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) and div g is bounded, dominated convergence gives ∫ u div g = lim_j ∫ φ_{ε_j} u div g, because φ_ε → 1_U pointwise and u1_U = u a.e. (u = 0 a.e. off Ū, and Ū∖U = frontier U is Lⁿ-null for convex U, Mathlib Convex.addHaar_frontier). At points where φ_ε and g are differentiable (a.e.), div(φ_ε g) = φ_ε div g + ∇φ_ε·g, so ∫ φ_ε u div g = ∫_U u div(φ_ε g) − ∫ u g·∇φ_ε ≤ |Du|(U) + ∫|u||∇φ_ε| (φ_ε g is admissible for U: Lipschitz, tsupport ⊆ U compact, |φ_εg| ≤ 1) ≤ (1 + δ⁻¹)|Du|(U) + nδ⁻¹R⁻¹∫_U|u| (C4) ≤ C(|Du|(U) + R⁻¹∫_U|u|). Hence ofReal(∫ u div g) ≤ ofReal C·(|Du|(U) + ofReal R⁻¹·∫⁻_U ‖u‖ₑ), and taking the supremum over g gives the second conjunct; C0 is the first. This proves BVExtensionEstimate.

Conclusion. Sections A, B, C prove the three conjuncts BVCompactness, BVPoincare, BVExtensionEstimate.

subproblem.title: Eilenberg inequality (Simon 2.1.9)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a σ-compact metric space, m ≥ 1 natural, k > 0 real, A ⊆ X 𝓗^{m+k}-null-measurable with 𝓗^{m+k}(A) < ∞ (Simon-normalized Hausdorff measures 𝓗^s = (ω_s/2^s)μH[s]) and f : X → ℝᵐ K-Lipschitz on A. Then y ↦ 𝓗^k(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable on ℝᵐ and ∫_{ℝᵐ} 𝓗^k(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dLᵐ(y) ≤ (ω_m ω_k/ω_{m+k}) K^m 𝓗^{m+k}(A).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §1, Theorem 1.9, Remark 1.10 and the printed proof (pp. 45-46). The printed proof leaves the measurability of y ↦ H^k(A ∩ f⁻¹y) as an exercise (Q.5 of hw2) and asserts that f(C_ij) is Borel; both points are completed below (the second is repaired by using closures of the images, which have the same diameter). The isodiametric inequality 2.10 of Ch. 1 is available as the kernel-checked SimonGMT theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_2_10: for every n and every A ⊆ ℝⁿ, volume A ≤ ω_n (diam A/2)^n (ediam, ENNReal). No other erratum.

Conventions. 𝓗^s := Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal s = c_s·μH[s], c_s = ω_s/2^s ∈ (0,∞), ω_s = Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume s. By Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_apply, μH[s](E) = sup_{δ>0} pre^s_δ(E), where pre^s_δ(E) := inf{Σ_l (diam C_l)^s : E ⊆ ∪_l C_l countable, diam C_l ≤ δ} (empty sets contribute 0), and pre^s_δ(E) increases as δ decreases. Put S^s_δ(E) := c_s pre^s_δ(E) = inf Σ_l ω_s(diam C_l/2)^s, so 𝓗^s(E) = sup_δ S^s_δ(E) = lim_{i→∞} S^s_{1/i}(E). Lᵐ = volume on ℝᵐ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m). Constant c := ω_m ω_k/ω_{m+k}.

PART I. PRINTED PROOF (cleaned transcription).
For each i = 1, 2, … pick closed subsets C_{i1}, C_{i2}, … with diam C_{ij} < 1/i, A ⊆ ∪_j C_{ij} and (1) Σ_j ω_{m+k}(diam C_{ij}/2)^{m+k} ≤ H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i, and let g_i be the Borel measurable simple functions g_i = Σ_j ω_k (diam C_{ij}/2)^k χ_{f(C_{ij})}. Notice that, by σ-compactness of X, each C_{ij} is a countable union of compact sets and hence indeed f(C_{ij}) is a Borel set and g_i is Borel measurable as claimed. Also notice that (2) g_i(y) = Σ_j ω_k(diam C_{ij}/2)^k χ_{f(C_{ij})}(y) = Σ_{j : f⁻¹y ∩ C_{ij} ≠ ∅} ω_k(diam C_{ij}/2)^k ≥ H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹y), and hence by integrating each side with respect to Lᵐ we have, by (1) and (2), ∫* H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹y) dLᵐ(y) ≤ ∫ g_i dLᵐ = Σ_j ω_k (diam C_{ij}/2)^k Lᵐ(f(C_{ij})) ≤ Σ_j ω_k ω_m (Lip f)^m (diam C_{ij}/2)^{m+k} ≤ (ω_mω_k/ω_{m+k})(Lip f)^m (H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i), where ∫* is the upper integral of Remark 1.10 and where we used Lᵐ(f(C_{ij})) ≤ ω_m(diam f(C_{ij})/2)^m (by the isodiametric inequality 2.10) ≤ ω_m (Lip f)^m (diam C_{ij}/2)^m. Letting i → ∞ we conclude ∫* H^k(A ∩ f⁻¹y) dLᵐ(y) ≤ (ω_mω_k/ω_{m+k})(Lip f)^m H^{m+k}(A). It remains to check that H^k(A ∩ f⁻¹y) is an Lᵐ-measurable function of y (exercise).

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF THE FROZEN STATEMENT.
Let X be a σ-compact metric space (Borel σ-algebra), m ≥ 1 natural, k > 0 real, A ⊆ X with NullMeasurableSet A 𝓗^{m+k}, 𝓗^{m+k}(A) < ∞, f : X → ℝᵐ with LipschitzOnWith K f A. Write Φ_E(y) := 𝓗^k(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}).

Step 1 (covering estimate, valid for every E ⊆ A with 𝓗^{m+k}(E) < ∞). Claim: there is a Borel function G_E : ℝᵐ → [0,∞] with Φ_E ≤ G_E everywhere and ∫ G_E dLᵐ ≤ c K^m 𝓗^{m+k}(E).
1. Fix such an E (it will be used for E = A and for an 𝓗^{m+k}-null subset N ⊆ A); f is K-Lipschitz on E. The case K = 0 is included (then every T_{i,l} below is a point or empty and has Lᵐ-measure 0 because m ≥ 1).
2. For i ≥ 1 choose (definition of pre^{m+k}_{1/i}(E) < ∞) sets C_{i,l}, l ≥ 1, with E ⊆ ∪_l C_{i,l}, diam C_{i,l} ≤ 1/i and Σ_l ω_{m+k}(d_{i,l}/2)^{m+k} ≤ S^{m+k}_{1/i}(E) + 1/i ≤ 𝓗^{m+k}(E) + 1/i, where d_{i,l} := diam C_{i,l}.
3. Let T_{i,l} := closure f(C_{i,l} ∩ E) (closed, hence Borel). Since f is K-Lipschitz on E, diam T_{i,l} = diam f(C_{i,l} ∩ E) ≤ K d_{i,l}. Define the Borel function G_i(y) := Σ_l ω_k (d_{i,l}/2)^k 1_{T_{i,l}}(y).
4. Pointwise bound: for every y, the sets C_{i,l} ∩ E ∩ f⁻¹{y} (l ≥ 1) cover E ∩ f⁻¹{y}, have diameter ≤ d_{i,l} ≤ 1/i, and are empty unless y ∈ f(C_{i,l} ∩ E) ⊆ T_{i,l}. Hence S^k_{1/i}(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ Σ_{l : y ∈ T_{i,l}} ω_k(d_{i,l}/2)^k = G_i(y).
5. Integral bound: by the isodiametric inequality (SimonGMT simon_theorem_2_10) Lᵐ(T_{i,l}) ≤ ω_m (diam T_{i,l}/2)^m ≤ ω_m K^m (d_{i,l}/2)^m, hence ∫ G_i dLᵐ = Σ_l ω_k(d_{i,l}/2)^k Lᵐ(T_{i,l}) ≤ ω_mω_k K^m Σ_l (d_{i,l}/2)^{m+k} = c K^m Σ_l ω_{m+k}(d_{i,l}/2)^{m+k} ≤ c K^m (𝓗^{m+k}(E) + 1/i). (ENNReal arithmetic: (Kd/2)^m = K^m (d/2)^m for natural m, and (d/2)^k (d/2)^m = (d/2)^{k+m}, valid also for d = 0 because k > 0.)
6. Put G_E := liminf_i G_i (Borel). For every y, Φ_E(y) = sup_i S^k_{1/i}(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = lim_i S^k_{1/i}(E ∩ f⁻¹{y}) (monotone in i) ≤ liminf_i G_i(y) = G_E(y) by step 4. By Fatou's lemma, ∫ G_E ≤ liminf_i ∫ G_i ≤ c K^m 𝓗^{m+k}(E) by step 5.
7. Consequence: if 𝓗^{m+k}(E) = 0 then G_E is a Borel function with integral 0, so G_E = 0 Lᵐ-a.e., hence Φ_E(y) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y.

Step 2 (measurability for compact sets). Claim: for compact Q ⊆ A, y ↦ Φ_Q(y) is Borel.
8. For δ > 0 and compact F ⊆ X let U_δ(F) := inf{Σ_{l=1}^p (diam O_l)^k : p ∈ ℕ, O_l ⊆ X open, diam O_l < δ, F ⊆ ∪_{l≤p} O_l} (finite open covers; such covers exist by compactness, using open balls of radius < δ/2).
9. pre^k_δ(F) ≤ U_δ(F): a finite open cover by sets of diameter < δ is an admissible countable cover.
10. U_{2δ}(F) ≤ pre^k_δ(F): let ε > 0 and {C_l} a countable cover of F with diam C_l ≤ δ and Σ_l (diam C_l)^k ≤ pre^k_δ(F) + ε (discard empty C_l). Since k > 0, t ↦ t^k is continuous, so we can choose η_l ∈ (0, δ/2) with (diam C_l + 2η_l)^k ≤ (diam C_l)^k + ε2^{−l}. The open sets O_l := {x : dist(x, C_l) < η_l} cover F, have diam O_l ≤ diam C_l + 2η_l < 2δ, and by compactness finitely many of them cover F; so U_{2δ}(F) ≤ Σ_l (diam C_l + 2η_l)^k ≤ pre^k_δ(F) + 2ε.
11. Upper semicontinuity: for fixed δ, y ↦ U_δ(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is upper semicontinuous on ℝᵐ. Indeed, if U_δ(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y₀}) < t, choose a finite open cover O_1,…,O_p of Q ∩ f⁻¹{y₀} with diam O_l < δ and Σ(diam O_l)^k < t. The set Q∖∪O_l is compact, f is continuous on Q (Lipschitz on A ⊇ Q), so f(Q∖∪O_l) is compact and does not contain y₀; choose ρ > 0 with B(y₀,ρ) ∩ f(Q∖∪O_l) = ∅. For |y − y₀| < ρ, Q ∩ f⁻¹{y} ⊆ ∪O_l, hence U_δ(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) < t. So {y : U_δ(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) < t} is open and U_δ(Q ∩ f⁻¹(·)) is Borel.
12. By steps 9-10, pre^k_{1/i} ≤ U_{1/i} ≤ pre^k_{1/(2i)} ≤ μH[k] on compact sets, hence μH[k](Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = sup_i pre^k_{1/i}(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = sup_i U_{1/i}(Q ∩ f⁻¹{y}) (Q ∩ f⁻¹{y} is compact: closed in Q). Thus Φ_Q = c_k sup_i U_{1/i}(Q ∩ f⁻¹(·)) is Borel.

Step 3 (inner approximation). 13. Exactly as in Theorem 1.8 (finite Borel measure 𝓗^{m+k} restricted to a Borel A₀ ⊆ A with 𝓗^{m+k}(A∖A₀) = 0 is inner regular by compact sets on the σ-compact metric space X) there are compact Q_1 ⊆ Q_2 ⊆ … ⊆ A (take finite unions) with 𝓗^{m+k}(N) = 0, N := A∖∪_j Q_j.

Step 4 (measurability of Φ_A). 14. Let Q_∞ := ∪_j Q_j. For each y, (Q_j ∩ f⁻¹{y})_j increases to Q_∞ ∩ f⁻¹{y}, so Φ_{Q_∞}(y) = sup_j Φ_{Q_j}(y) (continuity from below of the measure 𝓗^k), a Borel function of y by step 12. For each y, Φ_{Q_∞}(y) ≤ Φ_A(y) ≤ Φ_{Q_∞}(y) + Φ_N(y) (monotonicity and subadditivity), and Φ_N = 0 Lᵐ-a.e. by step 7 (f is K-Lipschitz on N ⊆ A and 𝓗^{m+k}(N) = 0). Hence Φ_A = Φ_{Q_∞} Lᵐ-a.e., so AEMeasurable Φ_A volume.

Step 5 (inequality). 15. By step 1 with E = A, Φ_A ≤ G_A pointwise with ∫ G_A ≤ c K^m 𝓗^{m+k}(A); by monotonicity of the lintegral, ∫⁻ y, 𝓗^k(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dLᵐ ≤ (ω_m ω_k/ω_{m+k}) K^m 𝓗^{m+k}(A), which in the frozen notation is ω[(m:ℝ)] * ω[k] / ω[m + k] * K^m * 𝓗[m + k] A (multiplication in ENNReal is commutative; ω_{m+k} ∈ (0,∞)).
16. Steps 14 and 15 are the two conclusions of EilenbergInequality.

subproblem.title: Lipschitz extension (Simon 2.1.2) and Rademacher theorem (Simon 2.1.4)
subproblem.statement: (1.2) For every metric space X (Lean X : Type with MetricSpace X), every nonempty A ⊆ X and every f : A → ℝ that is Lipschitz for the subspace metric (LipschitzWith K f for some K : ℝ≥0), there is F : X → ℝ which is Lipschitz (∃ K, LipschitzWith K F), has the same least Lipschitz constant, lipConst F = lipConst f where lipConst g := sInf {K : ℝ≥0 | LipschitzWith K g}, and satisfies F a = f a for all a ∈ A. (1.4) For every n ∈ ℕ and every Lipschitz f : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), f is Fréchet differentiable at volume-almost every point of ℝⁿ.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §1, printed proofs of Theorem 1.2 (p. 40) and Theorem 1.4 (pp. 40-42). No erratum affects these two items. The printed proofs are transcribed first (Part I); Part II is the complete numbered proof of the exact frozen statement LipschitzExtension ∧ Rademacher, following the printed route.

PART I. PRINTED PROOFS (cleaned transcription).

Theorem 1.2. If A is a non-empty subset of X and f : A → ℝ is Lipschitz, then there is f̄ : X → ℝ with Lip f̄ = Lip f and f = f̄|A.
Proof (printed). With L = Lip f, we claim that f̄(x) = inf_{z∈A} (f(z) + L d(x,z)), x ∈ X, has the required properties. Indeed if x ∈ A then trivially f̄(x) ≤ f(x) and also f̄(x) − f(x) = inf_{z∈A}(f(z) − f(x) + L d(x,z)) ≥ inf_{z∈A}(−L d(x,z) + L d(x,z)) = 0, so f̄(x) = f(x). Also for any x1, x2 ∈ X, f̄(x1) − f̄(x2) = sup_{z2∈A} inf_{z1∈A}(f(z1) + L d(x1,z1) − f(z2) − L d(x2,z2)) ≤ sup_{z2∈A}(L d(x1,z2) − L d(x2,z2)) ≤ L d(x1,x2), and the reverse inequality holds by interchanging x1, x2.

Theorem 1.4 (Rademacher). If f is Lipschitz on ℝⁿ then f is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e.
Proof (printed, due to C. B. Morrey). For v ∈ S^{n−1} let D_v f(x) = d/dt f(x+tv)|_{t=0} whenever it exists. Since |f(y)−f(x)|/|y−x| ≤ Lip f, |D_v f| ≤ Lip f, and D_v f(x) exists exactly when limsup_{t→0} and liminf_{t→0} of (f(x+tv)−f(x))/t coincide; both are Borel (limits of lower/upper semicontinuous sup/inf over 0<|t|<1/j), so A_v = {x : D_v f(x) does not exist} is Borel. For fixed x, v the function t ↦ f(x+tv) is absolutely continuous, hence differentiable for a.e. t, so A_v meets every line parallel to v in an H¹-null set, and by Fubini Lⁿ(A_v) = 0, i.e. (1) D_v f exists a.e. For φ ∈ C¹_c(ℝⁿ) and h > 0, (2) ∫ (f(x+hv)−f(x))/h · φ(x) dx = ∫ (φ(x)−φ(x−hv))/h · f(x) dx (change of variables), and by dominated convergence and (1), (3) ∫ D_v f φ = −∫ f D_v φ = −∫ f v·∇φ = Σ_j v^j ∫ D_j f φ = ∫ v·∇f φ, using Fubini and absolute continuity on lines for the integration by parts. Since φ is arbitrary, (4) D_v f(x) = v·∇f(x) for a.e. x, for each v, and (5) |∇f(x)| = sup_{|v|=1} D_v f(x) ≤ L at such points. With v_1, v_2, … dense in S^{n−1} and A_k = {x : ∇f(x), D_{v_k} f(x) exist and D_{v_k} f(x) = v_k·∇f(x)}, A = ∩_k A_k has (6) Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) = 0. For x ∈ A, v ∈ S^{n−1}, h ≠ 0 put (7) Q(x,v,h) = (f(x+hv)−f(x))/h − v·∇f(x); then (8) Q(x,v_j,h) → 0 as h → 0. Given ε > 0 choose P with (9) S^{n−1} ⊆ ∪_{i≤P} B_ε(v_i) and δ_i with (10) 0 < |h| < δ_i ⇒ |Q(x,v_i,h)| < ε. For v ∈ S^{n−1} pick i ≤ P with |v−v_i| < ε; then |Q(x,v,h)| ≤ |Q(x,v,h)−Q(x,v_i,h)| + |Q(x,v_i,h)| ≤ |h|^{−1}|f(x+hv)−f(x+hv_i)| + |v−v_i||∇f(x)| + |Q(x,v_i,h)| < (2L+1)ε for 0 < |h| < δ = min δ_i, by (5). Hence f is differentiable at every x ∈ A.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF THE FROZEN STATEMENT.

Notation. For a map g between pseudo-(e)metric spaces, lipConst g = sInf {K ∈ ℝ≥0 : LipschitzWith K g} (the contract definition; it is literally the same expression as the SimonGMT definition Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.optimalLipschitzConstant, so the two are definitionally equal).

A. Theorem 1.2 (LipschitzExtension).
1. Let X be a metric space, A ⊆ X nonempty, f : A → ℝ with LipschitzWith K₀ f for some K₀ (A carries the subspace metric, dist(a,b) = d(a,b)). Put L := lipConst f.
2. f is L-Lipschitz (the infimum is attained). The set S = {K : LipschitzWith K f} is nonempty (K₀ ∈ S) and upward closed. For a, b ∈ A the inequality |f a − f b| ≤ K d(a,b) holds for every K ∈ S; choosing K_j ∈ S with K_j → L = inf S (property of the infimum in ℝ≥0) and letting j → ∞ gives |f a − f b| ≤ L d(a,b). (This is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.lipschitzWith_optimalLipschitzConstant.)
3. Define F(x) := inf_{a∈A} (f(a) + L d(x,a)) for x ∈ X. The infimum is finite: fixing a₀ ∈ A (A ≠ ∅), for every a ∈ A, f(a) + L d(x,a) ≥ f(a₀) − L d(a,a₀) + L d(x,a) ≥ f(a₀) − L d(x,a₀) by step 2 and the triangle inequality, so the set of values is bounded below and nonempty.
4. F = f on A: for x ∈ A, choosing a = x gives F(x) ≤ f(x); and for every a ∈ A, f(a) + L d(x,a) ≥ f(x) by step 2, so F(x) ≥ f(x).
5. F is L-Lipschitz: for x1, x2 ∈ X and a ∈ A, f(a) + L d(x1,a) ≤ f(a) + L d(x2,a) + L d(x1,x2); taking the infimum over a gives F(x1) ≤ F(x2) + L d(x1,x2), and symmetrically F(x2) ≤ F(x1) + L d(x1,x2). Hence LipschitzWith L F; in particular ∃ K, LipschitzWith K F.
6. lipConst F = L. (≤) L belongs to {K : LipschitzWith K F} by step 5, so the infimum lipConst F ≤ L. (≥) If LipschitzWith K F then for a, b ∈ A, |f a − f b| = |F a − F b| ≤ K d(a,b) by step 4, i.e. LipschitzWith K f, so K ≥ lipConst f = L; taking the infimum over such K gives lipConst F ≥ L.
7. Steps 4-6 give the three required conclusions. (Formal route: the SimonGMT theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.lipschitz_extension_real_optimal (hA : A.Nonempty) (f : A → ℝ) (hf : IsLipschitz f) returns exactly F with IsLipschitz F (= ∃ K, LipschitzWith K F), F x = f x on A, and optimalLipschitzConstant F = optimalLipschitzConstant f; these are the frozen conclusions after unfolding the definitionally equal names. Alternatively Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.extend_real applied to the function x ↦ (if h : x ∈ A then f ⟨x,h⟩ else 0), which is L-Lipschitz on A, gives F with LipschitzWith L F and F = f on A, and step 6 finishes.)

B. Theorem 1.4 (Rademacher).
8. Let n ∈ ℕ and f : ℝⁿ → ℝ with LipschitzWith K f, where ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and Lⁿ = volume.
9. Lebesgue measure volume on the finite-dimensional real normed space ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure.
10. Morrey's argument of Part I proves that the set of points where f is not Fréchet differentiable is Lⁿ-null: steps (1)-(6) produce a full-measure set A on which the gradient ∇f and the directional derivatives along a countable dense set of directions exist and agree with v·∇f, and steps (7)-(10) show that at every x ∈ A the difference quotients converge to v·∇f(x) uniformly in v ∈ S^{n−1}, which is Fréchet differentiability with derivative h ↦ ∇f(x)·h.
11. subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure of Lipschitz images and multiplicity bound (Simon 2.1.8)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a σ-compact metric space and Y a metric space (Borel σ-algebras), m ≥ 0 real, 𝓗^m = (ω_m/2^m)μH[m] Simon-normalized Hausdorff measure, A ⊆ X 𝓗^m-null-measurable with 𝓗^m(A) < ∞, and f : X → Y K-Lipschitz on A. Then (i) f(A) is 𝓗^m-null-measurable and 𝓗^m(f(A)) ≤ K^m 𝓗^m(A); (ii) the multiplicity N(y) = encard(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) is 𝓗^m-a.e.-measurable on Y and ∫_Y N d𝓗^m ≤ K^m 𝓗^m(A).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §1, Theorem 1.8 and its printed proof (pp. 44-45). No erratum. Formal conventions of the frozen statement: 𝓗^m := Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal m = c_m·μH[m] with c_m = ω_m/2^m ∈ (0,∞) (Mathlib μH[m] = hausdorffMeasure m); Carathéodory 𝓗^m-measurability is rendered NullMeasurableSet / AEMeasurable; the Lipschitz constant K ∈ ℝ≥0 plays the role of Lip f (K^m is ENNReal.rpow); N(f,y) = fiberCount A f y = encard(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ∈ [0,∞].

PART I. PRINTED PROOF (cleaned transcription).
(i) Observe first that if δ > 0 and C₁, C₂, … are chosen with A ⊆ ∪_j C_j and diam C_j < δ for each j, then f(A) ⊆ ∪_j f(C_j) and diam f(C_j) ≤ (Lip f)δ < (1 + Lip f)δ. Hence H^m_{(1+Lip f)δ}(f(A)) ≤ Σ_j ω_m (diam f(C_j)/2)^m ≤ (Lip f)^m Σ_j ω_m (diam C_j/2)^m, and taking inf over all such collections {C_j} and then letting δ ↓ 0 we obtain H^m(f(A)) ≤ (Lip f)^m H^m(A). Notice this part of the argument is valid even if A is not H^m-measurable and did not depend on the σ-compactness of X. Next suppose that A is H^m-measurable and observe that the regularity property 1.15(2) of Ch. 1 together with the σ-compactness of X implies that we can take a sequence K₁, K₂, … of compact sets in X with K_j ⊆ A for each j and H^m(A∖(∪_j K_j)) = 0. By the first part above we then have H^m(f(A∖(∪_j K_j))) = 0 and hence f(A) = f(A∖(∪_j K_j)) ∪ (∪_j f(K_j)). Now f(K_j) is compact, hence Borel, for each j, and H^m(f(A∖(∪_j K_j))) ≤ (Lip f)^m H^m(A∖(∪_j K_j)) = 0, so f(A) is H^m-measurable as claimed.
(ii) By the σ-compactness of X, for each i = 1, 2, … we can partition A into a disjoint union ∪_{j=1}^∞ A_{ij} where each A_{ij} is H^m-measurable and diam(A_{ij}) < 1/i; furthermore we can do this successively, partitioning each A_{ik} to give the new sets A_{i+1,j}, so that each of the sets A_{i+1,j} is contained in one of the A_{ik}. Observe that then Σ_j χ_{f(A_{ij})} is a non-negative function which is H^m-measurable by (i) and which increases pointwise (at every point) to N(f,y), and so N(f,y) is H^m-measurable and by the monotone convergence theorem ∫_Y N(f,y) dH^m(y) = lim_i ∫_Y Σ_j χ_{f(A_{ij})} dH^m = lim_i Σ_j H^m(f(A_{ij})), and Σ_j H^m(f(A_{ij})) ≤ (Lip f)^m Σ_j H^m(A_{ij}) = (Lip f)^m H^m(A) by part (i).

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF THE FROZEN STATEMENT.
Let X be a σ-compact metric space and Y a metric space, both with their Borel σ-algebras, m ≥ 0 real, A ⊆ X with NullMeasurableSet A 𝓗^m and 𝓗^m(A) < ∞, f : X → Y with LipschitzOnWith K f A.

(i) Inequality.
1. For every set E ⊆ A: μH[m](f(E)) ≤ K^m μH[m](E). This is the covering argument of Part I; formally Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (needs 0 ≤ m), applied to f restricted to E (LipschitzOnWith K f E by monotonicity). Multiplying by c_m: 𝓗^m(f(E)) ≤ K^m 𝓗^m(E). With E = A this is the inequality in (i). In particular, if 𝓗^m(E) = 0 then 𝓗^m(f(E)) = 0 (K^m < ∞).

(i) Measurability.
2. Inner compact approximation. Since A is null-measurable there is a measurable (Borel) A₀ ⊆ A with 𝓗^m(A∖A₀) = 0 (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). The measure ν := 𝓗^m restricted to A₀ is a finite Borel measure on the σ-compact metric space X, hence inner regular with respect to compact sets on Borel sets (a finite Borel measure on a metric space is inner regular by closed sets; intersecting a closed set with the members of an increasing compact exhaustion of X gives compact sets whose measures converge). So for every j there is a compact Q_j ⊆ A₀ with 𝓗^m(A₀∖Q_j) < 1/j. Let A₁ := ∪_j Q_j ⊆ A; then 𝓗^m(A∖A₁) ≤ 𝓗^m(A∖A₀) + 𝓗^m(A₀∖Q_j) < 1/j for all j, so 𝓗^m(A∖A₁) = 0. (This is exactly the argument of SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.nullMeasurableSet_image_of_lipschitzOn_sigmaCompact(_of_nullMeasurable), there written for natural m; it transfers verbatim to real m with 𝓗^m in place of μHE[n].)
3. f(A) = (∪_j f(Q_j)) ∪ f(A∖A₁). Each f(Q_j) is compact (f is continuous on Q_j ⊆ A), hence closed, hence Borel in Y; and 𝓗^m(f(A∖A₁)) = 0 by step 1. A Borel set union a null set is null-measurable, so NullMeasurableSet (f(A)) 𝓗^m.
4. Steps 2-3 apply to any null-measurable E ⊆ A with 𝓗^m(E) < ∞ (with f still K-Lipschitz on E): f(E) is 𝓗^m-null-measurable.

(ii) Multiplicity.
5. Nested countable Borel partitions. X is σ-compact metric, hence separable; let {q_l} be a countable dense subset. For i ≥ 1 and l ≥ 1 put Q_{i,l} := B(q_l, 1/(3i)) ∖ ∪_{l′<l} B(q_{l′}, 1/(3i)); for fixed i these are disjoint Borel sets covering X with diam Q_{i,l} ≤ 2/(3i) < 1/i. Let {P_{i,j}}_j be the nonempty sets among Q_{1,l₁} ∩ … ∩ Q_{i,l_i} (countably many). Then {P_{i,j}}_j is a countable partition of X into Borel sets of diameter < 1/i, and every P_{i+1,j′} is contained in a unique P_{i,j}.
6. Pieces. A_{i,j} := A ∩ P_{i,j}: null-measurable, 𝓗^m(A_{i,j}) ≤ 𝓗^m(A) < ∞, pairwise disjoint in j, ∪_j A_{i,j} = A, and each A_{i,j} is the disjoint union of the A_{i+1,j′} with P_{i+1,j′} ⊆ P_{i,j}. By step 4, every f(A_{i,j}) is null-measurable.
7. Counting functions. N_i(y) := Σ_j 1_{f(A_{i,j})}(y) = #{j : A_{i,j} ∩ f⁻¹{y} ≠ ∅}. Each N_i is AEMeasurable for 𝓗^m (countable sum of indicators of null-measurable sets).
 (a) N_i ≤ N_{i+1}: if A_{i,j} meets f⁻¹{y}, one of its sub-pieces A_{i+1,j′} does, and distinct j give distinct j′.
 (b) N_i(y) ≤ fiberCount A f y: choosing one point of A ∩ f⁻¹{y} in each piece A_{i,j} that meets f⁻¹{y} defines an injection (pieces are disjoint).
 (c) sup_i N_i(y) = fiberCount A f y: if F ⊆ A ∩ f⁻¹{y} is finite with #F = p, let 1/i be smaller than the least distance between distinct points of F; then distinct points of F lie in distinct pieces A_{i,j} (diam < 1/i), so N_i(y) ≥ p. Taking the supremum over finite F gives sup_i N_i(y) ≥ encard(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}), including the value ∞; with (b) equality holds.
8. AEMeasurability of fiberCount A f: it is the supremum of the countable family of AEMeasurable functions N_i (step 7c; Mathlib AEMeasurable.iSup / Measurable.iSup after choosing measurable modifications).
9. Integral bound. By monotone convergence for AEMeasurable functions (Mathlib lintegral_iSup′ with 7a), ∫ fiberCount A f d𝓗^m = lim_i ∫ N_i d𝓗^m, and ∫ N_i d𝓗^m = Σ_j 𝓗^m(f(A_{i,j})) (integral of a countable sum of indicators of null-measurable sets) ≤ Σ_j K^m 𝓗^m(A_{i,j}) (step 1) = K^m 𝓗^m(A) (countable additivity for disjoint null-measurable sets). Hence ∫_Y fiberCount A f d𝓗^m ≤ K^m 𝓗^m(A).
10. Steps 1, 3, 8 and 9 are the four conclusions of LipschitzImageHausdorff.
proof_key_steps: Image inequality from the covering argument (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le scaled by ω_m/2^m).
Inner regularity: compact Q_j ⊆ A with 𝓗^m(A∖∪Q_j) = 0 (finite Borel measure on a σ-compact metric space).
f(A) = ∪f(Q_j) (Borel) ∪ f(null set) (null), hence null-measurable.
Nested countable Borel partitions of X of mesh < 1/i give pieces A_{ij}; N_i = Σ_j 1_{f(A_ij)} is a.e.-measurable and increases to N.
Monotone convergence and (i) give ∫N = lim Σ_j 𝓗^m(f(A_ij)) ≤ K^m 𝓗^m(A).

subproblem.title: Tangent space equals range of the chart derivative; Simon submanifolds are Borel with continuous tangent projection (Simon 2.4.1-4.3)
subproblem.statement: (1) If 1 ≤ r and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ is a Simon local representation of M on (V, W) (V, W open, ψ C^r on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, relatively proper, Dψ injective on V), then for every x ∈ V the tangent space tangentSpace M (ψ x) (span of velocities of C¹ curves (−1,1) → M through ψ(x)) equals range Dψ(x). (2) If M is an n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ then M is a Borel set and y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous on M.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), 1 ≤ r → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap) ∧ ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → MeasurableSet M ∧ ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §4: definition 4.1 of a C^r submanifold (local representation ψ : V → W, 1:1, C^r, proper, Dψ of rank n), 4.2 (ψ is a homeomorphism onto M ∩ W, hence an open map onto its image), and 4.3 (T_yM is a linear subspace with basis D₁ψ(x), …, D_nψ(x)), p. 55. The printed text says only (One readily checks that) for 4.3 and (Indeed the above definition ensures the local representation ψ is a homeomorphism) for 4.2; complete proofs are given below for the exact frozen notions: tangentSpace M y := span{γ′(0) : γ : ℝ → E, C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = y}, tangentProjection M y := orthogonal projection onto tangentSpace M y, and SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation / IsSimonSubmanifold. This child is a shared lemma for the children variation_formulas, stationary_results, coarea_formula and c1_sard (they need T_yM = range Dψ, Borel measurability of M, and continuity of y ↦ P_y on M).

Statement. (1) For n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞ with 1 ≤ r, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ such that IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ (V, W open; ψ is C^r on V; ψ injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ M; for every compact Q ⊆ W the set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact; Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V), and every x ∈ V: tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x). (2) If M is an n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ (IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M: 1 ≤ r and every y ∈ M lies in W for some local representation (V, W, ψ)), then M is a Borel set and y ↦ tangentProjection M y ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) is continuous on M (relative topology).

Proof.

Part 1 (tangent space = range of the derivative).
Fix a representation (V, W, ψ) with r ≥ 1, x₀ ∈ V, y₀ := ψ(x₀), T := range Dψ(x₀). Since V is open and ψ is C^r with r ≥ 1 on V, ψ is differentiable at every point of V with derivative Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x, continuous in x.
1. ψ⁻¹ is continuous on W ∩ M (4.2). Let y_j → y in W ∩ M and x_j, x ∈ V the unique preimages. The set Q := {y_j : j} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact and contains all x_j. Every subsequence of (x_j) has a further subsequence converging to some x′ ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) ⊆ V, and ψ(x′) = lim ψ(x_j) = y by continuity, so x′ = x by injectivity; hence x_j → x. (Formal reference: SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.isEmbedding_chartMap; the open-map form is IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter: every open V₀ ⊆ V has ψ(V₀) = W₀ ∩ M for an open W₀ ⊆ W.)
2. T ⊆ tangentSpace M y₀. Let w ∈ ℝⁿ, w ≠ 0 (w = 0 is trivial). Choose ρ > 0 with B(x₀, ρ) ⊆ V and put c := ρ/(2|w|) and γ(t) := ψ(x₀ + ctw), t ∈ ℝ. For t ∈ (−1,1), x₀ + ctw ∈ B(x₀, ρ/2) ⊆ V, so γ(t) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M; γ is C¹ on (−1,1) (composition of the C^r map ψ on the open set V with an affine map); γ(0) = y₀; and γ′(0) = c·Dψ(x₀)w by the chain rule. Thus c·Dψ(x₀)w is a generator of tangentSpace M y₀, and so is Dψ(x₀)w after multiplying by c⁻¹ (span). Hence T ⊆ tangentSpace M y₀.
3. tangentSpace M y₀ ⊆ T. Since T is a linear subspace it suffices to show that every generator v lies in T. Let γ be C¹ on (−1,1) with γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = y₀, HasDerivAt γ v 0.
 (i) W is open and γ is continuous at 0 with γ(0) = y₀ ∈ W, so there is τ ∈ (0,1) with γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M for |t| < τ. Put c(t) := ψ⁻¹(γ(t)) ∈ V for |t| < τ; c is continuous at 0 with c(0) = x₀ (step 1), and γ(t) = ψ(c(t)).
 (ii) Dψ(x₀) is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ, so there is λ > 0 with |Dψ(x₀)ζ| ≥ λ|ζ| for all ζ. By differentiability of ψ at x₀ and continuity of c at 0, for |t| small: |ψ(c(t)) − ψ(x₀) − Dψ(x₀)(c(t) − x₀)| ≤ (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀|, hence (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀| ≤ |γ(t) − γ(0)| ≤ (|v| + 1)|t| (differentiability of γ at 0). So ζ(t) := (c(t) − x₀)/t is bounded for small t ≠ 0.
 (iii) Choose t_j → 0, t_j ≠ 0, with ζ(t_j) → ζ (Bolzano-Weierstrass). Writing ψ(c(t_j)) − ψ(x₀) = Dψ(x₀)(c(t_j) − x₀) + e_j with |e_j| ≤ ε_j|c(t_j) − x₀|, ε_j → 0, we get (γ(t_j) − γ(0))/t_j = Dψ(x₀)ζ(t_j) + e_j/t_j and |e_j/t_j| ≤ ε_j·2(|v| + 1)/λ → 0. The left side tends to v, the right side to Dψ(x₀)ζ. Hence v = Dψ(x₀)ζ ∈ T.
4. Steps 2-3 give tangentSpace M (ψ x₀) = range Dψ(x₀) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀).toLinearMap. In particular it has dimension n.

Part 2 (measurability of M and continuity of the tangent projection).
Let M be an n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold (1 ≤ r).
5. Local closedness. Let (V, W, ψ) be a local representation. Then W ∩ M is closed in W: if z_j ∈ W ∩ M and z_j → z ∈ W, the compact set Q := {z_j} ∪ {z} ⊆ W has compact V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) containing x_j := ψ⁻¹(z_j); a subsequence converges to some x ∈ V with ψ(x) = z, so z ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M. Hence W ∩ M = W ∩ F_W with F_W := closure(W ∩ M).
6. M is Borel. The open sets W_y (y ∈ M; W_y from a local representation with y ∈ W_y) cover M; ℝᴺ is second countable, so countably many of them, W_1, W_2, …, cover M (Lindelöf). subproblem.title: Whitney extension theorem for C¹ jets (Simon 2.1.6)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, closed A ⊆ ℝⁿ, h : ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous on A and ν : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ continuous on A such that for every compact K ⊆ A and every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ ε|y − x| for all x ∈ K and y ∈ A with 0 < |y − x| < δ, there is a C¹ function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with g(x) = h(x) and Dg(x)v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for all x ∈ A and v ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §1, Theorem 1.6 (pp. 42-43). The book gives no proof in general: it says (For the proof see for example [EG92] or [Fed69]; for the case n = 1 see Remark 1.7(2)). Remark 1.7(2) (printed) treats n = 1: ℝ∖A is a countable union of disjoint open intervals I_j = (a,b), on each of which one chooses g_j ∈ C¹[a,b] with g_j(a) = h(a), g_j(b) = h(b), g_j′(a) = ν(a), g_j′(b) = ν(b) and sup_{I_j}|g_j′ − ν(a)| ≤ 3ε_C(b−a), and sets g = g_j on I_j, g = h on A. Below we supply the complete proof in every dimension, following the cited reference [EG92] (Evans-Gariepy, Whitney's extension theorem): a Whitney-type covering of ℝⁿ∖A, a partition of unity with derivative bounds ≲ 1/dist(·,A), and the averaged first-order Taylor polynomials of h at nearest points of A. No erratum applies.

Statement being proved (exact frozen form). Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), A ⊆ ℝⁿ closed, h : ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous on A, ν : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ continuous on A, and assume
(W) for every compact K ⊆ A and every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that for all x ∈ K and all y ∈ A with 0 < |y − x| < δ: |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ ε|y − x|.
Then there is g : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ with g(x) = h(x) and Dg(x)v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for all x ∈ A, v ∈ ℝⁿ.

Proof.

0. Trivial cases and notation. If A = ∅ take g ≡ 0. Assume A ≠ ∅ from now on. Put U := ℝⁿ∖A (open), d(x) := dist(x, A) (1-Lipschitz, d > 0 exactly on U, and for every x there is a nearest point a ∈ A with |x − a| = d(x) since A is closed and nonempty in ℝⁿ), and r(x) := min{1, d(x)}/20, which is 1/20-Lipschitz. If U = ∅ (A = ℝⁿ) the construction below has no balls and g := h; the argument of steps 5-6 then applies verbatim (only the case x ∈ A occurs).

1. Covering. Apply the Vitali covering lemma (Mathlib: Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall with radii bounded by R = 1/20 and enlargement factor τ = 5 > 3) to the family of closed balls B̄(x, r(x)), x ∈ U. It yields a subfamily of pairwise disjoint balls B̄(s_j, r_j), r_j := r(s_j), j ∈ J, such that every B̄(x, r(x)) with x ∈ U is contained in some B̄(s_j, 5r_j). J is countable (pairwise disjoint sets with nonempty interior in the separable space ℝⁿ). In particular U = ∪_j B̄(s_j, 5r_j).

2. Geometry of the cover.
(F1) If |x − s_j| ≤ 10r_j then |r(x) − r_j| ≤ |x − s_j|/20 ≤ r_j/2, hence r_j/2 ≤ r(x) ≤ 3r_j/2, i.e. (2/3)r(x) ≤ r_j ≤ 2r(x); and since d(s_j) ≥ 20r_j (because r_j ≤ d(s_j)/20), d(x) ≥ d(s_j) − |x − s_j| ≥ 10r_j > 0, so x ∈ U.
(F2) For x ∈ U let J(x) := {j : |x − s_j| < 10r_j}. Then #J(x) ≤ N := 33ⁿ. Indeed for j ∈ J(x) the disjoint balls B̄(s_j, r_j) lie in B̄(x, 11r_j) ⊆ B̄(x, 22r(x)) and have radius r_j ≥ (2/3)r(x); comparing Lebesgue measures, #J(x)·((2/3)r(x))ⁿ ≤ (22r(x))ⁿ.
(F3) Local finiteness: for x₀ ∈ U only finitely many balls B(s_j, 10r_j) meet B(x₀, r(x₀)). If z lies in both, then r_j ≥ (2/3)r(z) ≥ (2/3)(19/20)r(x₀) ≥ r(x₀)/2 and r_j ≤ 2r(z) ≤ (21/10)r(x₀) < 3r(x₀), so B̄(s_j, r_j) ⊆ B̄(x₀, 34r(x₀)); disjointness and comparison of measures bound the number of such j by 68ⁿ.
(F4) For x ∈ U and j ∈ J(x), choose for every j a point a_j ∈ A with |s_j − a_j| = d(s_j) (fixed once and for all). Then |a_j − x| ≤ |a_j − s_j| + |s_j − x| = d(s_j) + |s_j − x| ≤ d(x) + 2|s_j − x| < d(x) + 20r_j ≤ d(x) + 40r(x) ≤ 3d(x), using r_j ≤ 2r(x) and r(x) ≤ d(x)/20.

3. Partition of unity. Fix θ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1, θ = 1 on B̄(0,5) and θ = 0 outside B(0,9) (a smooth bump, e.g. Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = 5, rOut = 9), and let Λ := sup|Dθ| < ∞. Put θ_j(x) := θ((x − s_j)/r_j): θ_j ∈ C^∞, θ_j = 1 on B̄(s_j, 5r_j), tsupport θ_j ⊆ B̄(s_j, 9r_j) ⊆ U, |Dθ_j| ≤ Λ/r_j. By (F3) the sum Σ(x) := Σ_j θ_j(x) is locally finite on U, hence C^∞ on U; Σ ≥ 1 on U (every x ∈ U lies in some B̄(s_j,5r_j)) and Σ ≤ N by (F2). Define v_j := θ_j/Σ on U. Then v_j ∈ C^∞(U), 0 ≤ v_j ≤ 1, Σ_j v_j = 1 on U, Σ_j Dv_j = 0 on U (derivative of a locally finite sum), v_j and Dv_j vanish at x ∈ U unless j ∈ J(x) (θ_j vanishes on a neighbourhood of x when |x − s_j| ≥ 10r_j > 9r_j), and for j ∈ J(x):
|Dv_j(x)| ≤ |Dθ_j(x)|/Σ(x) + θ_j(x)|DΣ(x)|/Σ(x)² ≤ Λ/r_j + Σ_{i∈J(x)} Λ/r_i ≤ (3/2)Λ(1 + N)/r(x) =: C₁/r(x),
using r_i ≥ (2/3)r(x) for i ∈ J(x).

4. Definition of g. Let P_j(x) := h(a_j) + ⟨ν(a_j), x − a_j⟩ (affine). Set g(x) := h(x) for x ∈ A and g(x) := Σ_j v_j(x)P_j(x) for x ∈ U. On U, g is a locally finite sum of C^∞ functions, hence C^∞, with Dg(x) = Σ_j P_j(x)Dv_j(x) + Σ_j v_j(x)⟨ν(a_j), ·⟩.

5. Estimates near a point a ∈ A. Fix a ∈ A, put K_a := A ∩ B̄(a, 4) (compact, contained in A) and let ω(t) := sup{|ν(p) − ν(q)| : p, q ∈ K_a, |p − q| ≤ t}, so ω(t) → 0 as t → 0 (uniform continuity of ν on the compact K_a). Given ε > 0 let δ_ε ∈ (0,1] be a δ given by (W) for the compact set K_a and ε.
(5a) First-order estimate. Let x ∈ ℝⁿ with |x − a| < δ_ε/4. If x ∈ A, x ≠ a, then by (W) (base point a ∈ K_a, y = x ∈ A): |g(x) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), x − a⟩| ≤ ε|x − a|. If x ∈ U then d(x) ≤ |x − a| and for j ∈ J(x), by (F4), |a_j − a| ≤ |a_j − x| + |x − a| ≤ 4|x − a| < δ_ε ≤ 1, so a_j ∈ K_a. Using Σ_j v_j(x) = 1,
g(x) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), x − a⟩ = Σ_{j∈J(x)} v_j(x)( [h(a_j) − h(a) − ⟨ν(a), a_j − a⟩] + ⟨ν(a_j) − ν(a), x − a_j⟩ ).
By (W) (base a, y = a_j; the bracket is 0 if a_j = a) the first bracket is ≤ ε|a_j − a| ≤ 4ε|x − a| in absolute value, and the second term is ≤ ω(4|x − a|)·3d(x) ≤ 3ω(4|x − a|)|x − a|. Hence |g(x) − g(a) − ⟨ν(a), x − a⟩| ≤ (4ε + 3ω(4|x − a|))|x − a| for all x with |x − a| < δ_ε/4. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and ω(t) → 0, g is differentiable at a with Dg(a)v = ⟨ν(a), v⟩ (and g(a) = h(a)).
(5b) Derivative estimate on U. Let x ∈ U with |x − a| < δ_ε/8 and let a* ∈ A with |x − a*| = d(x) ≤ |x − a|. Then |a* − a| ≤ 2|x − a| and, for j ∈ J(x), |a_j − a*| ≤ |a_j − x| + |x − a*| ≤ 4d(x) < δ_ε/2, and a*, a_j ∈ K_a. Let P*(x') := h(a*) + ⟨ν(a*), x' − a*⟩. Since Σ_j Dv_j(x) = 0,
Σ_j P_j(x)Dv_j(x) = Σ_{j∈J(x)} (P_j(x) − P*(x))Dv_j(x), and P_j(x) − P*(x) = [h(a_j) − h(a*) − ⟨ν(a*), a_j − a*⟩] + ⟨ν(a_j) − ν(a*), x − a_j⟩,
so by (W) (base a* ∈ K_a, y = a_j) and (F4), |P_j(x) − P*(x)| ≤ 4εd(x) + 3ω(4d(x))d(x). As d(x) < 1, r(x) = d(x)/20, so |Dv_j(x)| ≤ 20C₁/d(x), and with #J(x) ≤ N:
‖Σ_j P_j(x)Dv_j(x)‖ ≤ 20NC₁(4ε + 3ω(4d(x))).
Moreover |Σ_j v_j(x)ν(a_j) − ν(a)| = |Σ_{j∈J(x)} v_j(x)(ν(a_j) − ν(a))| ≤ ω(4|x − a|). Therefore
‖Dg(x) − ⟨ν(a), ·⟩‖ ≤ 20NC₁(4ε + 3ω(4|x − a|)) + ω(4|x − a|) for x ∈ U, |x − a| < δ_ε/8.

6. g is C¹ with the required values. g is differentiable at every point: on the open set U because it is C^∞ there, and at every a ∈ A by (5a), with Dg(a) = ⟨ν(a), ·⟩. Dg is continuous at every point of U (U open, g smooth there). Let a ∈ A and η > 0; choose ε > 0 with 80NC₁ε < η/3, then ρ ∈ (0, δ_ε/8) such that ω(4ρ)(60NC₁ + 1) < η/3 and such that |ν(x) − ν(a)| < η for x ∈ A ∩ B(a, ρ) (continuity of ν on A). For |x − a| < ρ: if x ∈ U, (5b) gives ‖Dg(x) − Dg(a)‖ < η; if x ∈ A, Dg(x) − Dg(a) = ⟨ν(x) − ν(a), ·⟩ has norm < η. So Dg is continuous on ℝⁿ, i.e. g is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 g ⇔ differentiable with continuous derivative). Finally g = h on A by definition and fderiv ℝ g x v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for x ∈ A by (5a). This proves WhitneyExtension.

Remarks for formalization. (i) The covering lemma, the bump function, local finiteness of the sum (finitely many nonzero terms on B(x₀, r(x₀))) and nearest points are standard Mathlib facts. (ii) Only the uniform hypothesis (W) on the single compact set K_a for each base point a is used, in the exact form of the frozen statement (base point in K, comparison point anywhere in A). (iii) The case n = 0 is covered: ℝ⁰ is a point, A = ∅ or A = ℝ⁰.

Vitali covering of U by disjoint balls B(s_j, r_j) with U covered by the 5-fold enlargements; bounded overlap (≤ 33ⁿ) and local finiteness of the 10-fold enlargements.
Smooth partition of unity v_j subordinate to B(s_j,10r_j) with Σv_j = 1, ΣDv_j = 0 and |Dv_j| ≤ C₁/r(x).
Define g = h on A and g = Σ v_j(h(a_j) + ⟨ν(a_j), x − a_j⟩) on U with a_j nearest points; nearby a_j satisfy |a_j − x| ≤ 3d(x).
Near a ∈ A, the uniform hypothesis on the compact K_a = A ∩ B̄(a,4) and uniform continuity of ν give the first-order estimate (g differentiable at a with Dg(a) = ν(a)) and Dg(x) → ν(a) for x ∈ U.
Hence g is differentiable everywhere with continuous derivative, i.e. C¹, with g = h and Dg = ⟨ν,·⟩ on A.

subproblem.title: C¹ approximation of Lipschitz functions (Simon 2.1.5)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every Lipschitz f : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every real ε > 0 there is g : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ such that the Lebesgue measure of {x : f(x) ≠ g(x)} ∪ {x : f does not have Fréchet derivative Dg(x) at x} is < ε.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §1, Theorem 1.5 and its printed proof (pp. 42-44). Erratum/reading applied (documented in GMT/Ch02/README.md): the set {∇f ≠ ∇g} is read as {x : not (f is differentiable at x with Df(x) = Dg(x))}, i.e. {x | ¬ HasFDerivAt f (fderiv ℝ g x) x}; it differs from the literal set by an Lⁿ-null set by Rademacher. Uses the sibling results Rademacher (child lipschitz_ext_rademacher, second conjunct) and WhitneyExtension (child whitney_extension).

PART I. PRINTED PROOF (cleaned transcription).
Proof of Theorem 1.5. By Rademacher's theorem f is differentiable on a set B ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖B) = 0. By Lusin's theorem (which applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ) there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that ∇f|C is continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) < ε/2. On C we define h(x) = f(x), ν(x) = ∇f(x) and R(x,y) for x, y ∈ C as in 1.6(*). Evidently (since C ⊆ B) lim_{y→x, y∈C} R(x,y) = 0 for every x ∈ C, but not necessarily uniformly with respect to x on compact subsets of C as in 1.6(*). We therefore proceed as follows. For k = 1, 2, … let η_k(x) = sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C ∩ B_{1/k}(x)∖{x}}. Then η_k ↓ 0 pointwise in C, and hence by Egoroff's theorem (applied to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0), j = 1, 2, …) there is an Lⁿ-measurable set A′ ⊆ C such that Lⁿ(C∖A′) < ε/4 and η_k converges uniformly to zero on each bounded subset of A′. Since we can take a closed set A ⊆ A′ with Lⁿ(A′∖A) < ε/4 we thus have Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) < ε and 1.6(*) holds. Hence we can apply the Whitney Theorem 1.6, and the proof is complete.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF THE FROZEN STATEMENT.
Statement: for every n ∈ ℕ, every Lipschitz f : ℝⁿ → ℝ (LipschitzWith K f) and every real ε > 0 there is g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ 1 g and volume({x | f x ≠ g x} ∪ {x | ¬ HasFDerivAt f (fderiv ℝ g x) x}) < ENNReal.ofReal ε. Here ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Lⁿ = volume.

0. The case n = 0. Then ℝ⁰ is a single point, so f is constant and every function on ℝ⁰ is C¹; take g := f. The set {x | f x ≠ g x} is empty and HasFDerivAt f (fderiv ℝ g x) x holds trivially (both sides are maps on a zero-dimensional space and f = g), so the exceptional set is empty and has measure 0 < ENNReal.ofReal ε. (Note that volume on ℝ⁰ is the Dirac mass at 0, of total mass 1, so this case must be treated separately.) From now on n ≥ 1.
1. Differentiability set. B := {x : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x} is a Borel set (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖B) = 0 by Rademacher (sibling conjunct; Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt).
2. Gradient field. Let ν(x) ∈ ℝⁿ be the vector with ⟨ν(x), v⟩ = fderiv ℝ f x v for all v (the gradient; ν(x) = 0 where f is not differentiable). ν is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv composed with the continuous linear isometry between the dual and ℝⁿ), and |ν(x)| ≤ K because ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ K for a K-Lipschitz f.
3. Lusin step: there is a closed C ⊆ B with ν|C continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) < ε/2. Construction: let S_1 := {x : |x| < 1} and S_j := {x : j − 1 < |x| < j} for j ≥ 2 (open, bounded, pairwise disjoint) and Z := ∪_{j≥1} {x : |x| = j} (Lⁿ-null since n ≥ 1); then ℝⁿ = Z ∪ ∪_j S_j. For each j and each coordinate i ≤ n apply the finite-measure Lusin theorem (SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, whose regularity hypothesis for Lebesgue measure is Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt) to the Borel function ⟨ν, e_i⟩ on the bounded Borel set S_j ∩ B, with error ε2^{−j−2}/(n+1); intersecting the n closed sets obtained gives a closed C_j ⊆ S_j ∩ B with Lⁿ((S_j ∩ B)∖C_j) < ε2^{−j−2} and ν|C_j continuous. Put C := ∪_j C_j. The family {C_j} is locally finite (a bounded set meets only finitely many S_j), so C is closed. ν|C is continuous: a point x ∈ C lies in exactly one C_j, and the open set S_j ∋ x satisfies S_j ∩ C = C_j, so continuity on C at x reduces to continuity on C_j. Finally Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖B) + Lⁿ(Z) + Σ_j Lⁿ((S_j∩B)∖C_j) < 0 + 0 + ε/4 < ε/2.
4. Remainders. For x ≠ y put R(x,y) := (f(y) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩)/|y − x|, so |R| ≤ 2K. For k ≥ 1 define η_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} for x ∈ C (sup ∅ := 0) and η_k(x) := 0 for x ∉ C.
 (a) 0 ≤ η_{k+1} ≤ η_k ≤ 2K.
 (b) η_k(x) → 0 for every x ∈ C: x ∈ B, so f is differentiable at x with derivative ⟨ν(x), ·⟩, i.e. R(x,y) → 0 as y → x.
 (c) Each η_k is Borel measurable. Let D ⊆ C be countable and dense in C. For fixed x ∈ C, y ↦ |R(x,y)| is continuous on ℝⁿ∖{x} and {y ∈ C : 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} is relatively open in C, so D is dense in it; hence η_k(x) = sup_{q∈D} 1{0 < |q − x| < 1/k}·|R(x,q)|. For each fixed q the function x ↦ 1_C(x)1{0 < |q − x| < 1/k}|R(x,q)| is Borel (f continuous, ν Borel), and a countable supremum of Borel functions is Borel.
5. Egorov step. For j ≥ 1 let C′_j := C ∩ {x : j − 1 ≤ |x| < j} (Borel, finite measure). By Egorov's theorem (Mathlib MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto, applied on C′_j to the strongly measurable η_k and the limit 0, using 4(b)) there is a measurable t_j ⊆ C′_j with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ ε2^{−j−4} and η_k → 0 uniformly on A′_j := C′_j∖t_j. Put A′ := ∪_j A′_j ⊆ C. Then Lⁿ(C∖A′) ≤ Σ_j Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ ε/16 < ε/8, and every bounded subset of A′ lies in A′_1 ∪ … ∪ A′_J for some J, on which η_k → 0 uniformly.
6. Closed inner approximation. For each j choose a closed F_j ⊆ A′_j with Lⁿ(A′_j∖F_j) < ε2^{−j−4} (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt; Lebesgue measure is weakly regular). Since F_j ⊆ {j − 1 ≤ |x| < j}, the family {F_j} is locally finite, so A := ∪_j F_j is closed, A ⊆ A′ ⊆ C ⊆ B and Lⁿ(A′∖A) < ε/8. Therefore Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) + Lⁿ(C∖A′) + Lⁿ(A′∖A) < ε/2 + ε/8 + ε/8 < ε.
7. Whitney hypotheses. Apply WhitneyExtension with this closed A, h := f and the field ν. h is continuous (f Lipschitz); ν is continuous on A ⊆ C (step 3). Let K ⊆ A be compact and ε′ > 0. K is bounded and contained in A′, so η_k → 0 uniformly on K: choose k with η_k(x) ≤ ε′ for all x ∈ K and put δ := 1/k. For x ∈ K and y ∈ A with 0 < |y − x| < δ we have y ∈ C, hence |R(x,y)| ≤ η_k(x) ≤ ε′, i.e. |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ ε′|y − x|. This is exactly hypothesis (W) of the frozen WhitneyExtension.
8. Conclusion. WhitneyExtension gives g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ 1 g, g(x) = f(x) and fderiv ℝ g x v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ for all x ∈ A, v ∈ ℝⁿ. For x ∈ A: f(x) = g(x), and since x ∈ B, f has derivative fderiv ℝ f x = ⟨ν(x), ·⟩ = fderiv ℝ g x at x, i.e. HasFDerivAt f (fderiv ℝ g x) x. Hence {x | f x ≠ g x} ∪ {x | ¬ HasFDerivAt f (fderiv ℝ g x) x} ⊆ ℝⁿ∖A, whose measure is < ε (step 6); since this measure is a real number < ε, it is < ENNReal.ofReal ε. This proves C1Approximation (the case n = 0 was treated in step 0).
proof_key_steps: Case n = 0: take g = f.
Rademacher: f is differentiable on a Borel set B of full measure; the gradient field ν is Borel and bounded.
Lusin on bounded shells: closed C ⊆ B with ν continuous on C and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) < ε/2.
The remainder suprema η_k (over a countable dense subset of C) are Borel, decrease to 0 on C; Egorov on shells gives A′ ⊆ C with Lⁿ(C∖A′) < ε/8 and uniform convergence on bounded subsets.
Closed A ⊆ A′ with Lⁿ(A′∖A) < ε/8, so Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) < ε.
The uniform convergence of η_k on compact subsets of A is exactly the Whitney hypothesis; Whitney gives g ∈ C¹ with g = f and Dg = Df on A, so the exceptional set lies in ℝⁿ∖A.
