subproblem.title: Co-area formula for C¹ maps on C¹ submanifolds (Simon 2.6.3, 2.6.6)
subproblem.statement: Let k ≥ 1, n = m + k, M an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ, U ⊇ M open, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ C¹ on U, and g : ℝᴺ → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ restricted to M. With J*f = coareaJacobian M f = √det(L L*), L = Df|_{T_xM}: y ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_M g J*f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dLᵐ(y) (Hᵈ = μHE[d]).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §6, 6.1-6.3 and 6.6 with the printed arguments (pp. 65-67). The book proves the linear case 6.2 and says of the general formula 6.3: (Its proof uses an approximation argument based on the linear case 6.2. See [Har79] or [Fed69] for the details); 6.6 is obtained (by applying 6.3 to a suitable increasing sequence of simple functions). A complete proof for C¹ maps on C¹ submanifolds is supplied below; it uses the linear algebra of 6.2, the implicit function theorem, the area formula and Fubini, and a direct covering estimate for the critical set. No erratum. Depends on the siblings area_formula and submanifold_tangent.

Statement (frozen CoareaFormula). N, m, k ∈ ℕ, k ≥ 1, n := m + k; M ⊆ ℝᴺ an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold; U ⊆ ℝᴺ open with M ⊆ U; f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on U; g : ℝᴺ → [0,∞] AEMeasurable for Hⁿ⌊M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then y ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ (Hᵏ = μHE[k]) is AEMeasurable for Lᵐ = volume, and ∫_M g·J*f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dLᵐ(y), where J*f(x) := coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L_xL_x*), L_x := Df(x)|_{T_xM} : T_xM → ℝᵐ.

PART I. PRINTED ARGUMENT (cleaned transcription).
6.1: for the orthogonal projection p : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ, Fubini gives ∫_{ℝᵐ} Hᵏ(p⁻¹(y) ∩ A) dLᵐ(y) = Hⁿ(A). 6.2: for a linear λ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ of rank m, let F = λ⁻¹(0) and choose an orthogonal q with q(F^⊥) = ℝᵐ × {0}, q(F) = {0} × ℝᵏ; then λ = σ∘p∘q with σ a linear isomorphism of ℝᵐ; by 6.1 and the change of variables z = σ(y), |det σ| Lⁿ(A) = ∫ Hᵏ(A ∩ λ⁻¹(z)) dLᵐ(z), and λλ* = σσ* gives |det σ| = √det(λλ*); so √det(λλ*) Lⁿ(A) = ∫_{ℝᵐ} Hᵏ(A ∩ λ⁻¹(y)) dLᵐ(y) (trivially valid, both sides 0, if rank λ < m). 6.3: for C¹ f : M → ℝᵐ and Borel A ⊆ M, ∫_A J*f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dLᵐ(y) (approximation argument based on 6.2, [Har79], [Fed69]). 6.6: for g ≥ 0 Hⁿ-measurable on M, ∫_M g J*f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{f⁻¹(y)} g dHᵏ dLᵐ(y) (apply 6.3 to an increasing sequence of simple functions).

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF.

Step 0 (preliminaries).
0.1 By submanifold_tangent: T_xM = range Dψ(x′) for every local representation ψ with ψ(x′) = x (dimension n); M is Borel; x ↦ P_x is continuous on M. Since L_xL_x* = Df(x)P_xDf(x)* as an endomorphism of ℝᵐ, J*f is continuous on M. Put C := {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0} (relatively closed in M, Borel) and R := M∖C (relatively open in M, Borel).
0.2 Linear algebra. (a) For L : T → ℝᵐ linear (T an inner product space), LL* is positive semidefinite, det(LL*) ≥ 0, and det(LL*) > 0 ⟺ L is surjective. (b) Lemma L: let T be an n-dimensional inner product space, L : T → ℝᵐ surjective, Θ : ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ → T a linear isomorphism with L(Θ(a,b)) = a for all (a,b), and Θ₂ := Θ(0,·) : ℝᵏ → T. Then √det(LL*)·√det(Θ*Θ) = √det(Θ₂*Θ₂). Proof: let Q := ker L (dim k) and Q^⊥ its orthogonal complement in T (dim m). L|_{Q^⊥} : Q^⊥ → ℝᵐ is an isomorphism and L* has range in Q^⊥, so √det(LL*) = |det L|_{Q^⊥}| (orthonormal bases). Θ₂ maps ℝᵏ isomorphically onto Q (LΘ(0,b) = 0). With respect to ℝᵐ ⊕ ℝᵏ and Q^⊥ ⊕ Q, Θ is block lower triangular with diagonal blocks α := π_{Q^⊥}Θ(·,0) and Θ₂, so √det(Θ*Θ) = |det Θ| = |det α|·|det Θ₂| (orthonormal bases); and L∘α = id_{ℝᵐ} because L(Θ(a,0)) = a and L vanishes on Q, so |det α| = 1/|det L|_{Q^⊥}|. Combining gives the claim, with |det Θ₂| = √det(Θ₂*Θ₂). (Cf. SimonGMT CoareaLinearAlgebra.lean and coarea_linear for 6.2.)

Step 1 (critical set: Hᵏ(C ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y).
1.1 Euclidean lemma. Let V ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, G : V → ℝᵐ of class C¹, C_G := {x ∈ V : rank DG(x) < m} (relatively closed in V), and Q ⊆ V compact. Then μHE[k](Q ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y.
Proof. If m = 0, C_G = ∅. Let m ≥ 1 and K′ := Q ∩ C_G (compact); if K′ = ∅ there is nothing to prove, so assume K′ ≠ ∅. Choose ρ₀ > 0 with K₁ := {x : dist(x,K′) ≤ ρ₀} ⊆ V (compact since K′ is compact and nonempty), L_G := max_{K₁}‖DG‖, ω(r) := sup{‖DG(z) − DG(x)‖ : x ∈ K′, |z − x| ≤ r} → 0 as r → 0 (uniform continuity on K₁). For x ∈ K′ and r ≤ ρ₀, the mean value inequality gives G(B̄(x,r)) ⊆ G(x) + DG(x)(B̄(0,r)) + B̄(0, ω(r)r). As rank DG(x) ≤ m − 1, pick a unit vector e orthogonal to range DG(x) and complete it to an orthonormal basis; then G(B̄(x,r)) lies in a box of side 2ω(r)r in direction e and sides 2(L_G + ω(r))r in the other m − 1 directions, so Lᵐ(G(B̄(x,r))) ≤ 2ᵐ ω(r)(L_G + ω(r))^{m−1} rᵐ. For 0 < r ≤ ρ₀ let x_1, …, x_p be a maximal r-separated subset of K′: the balls B̄(x_i, r) cover K′, and the disjoint balls B(x_i, r/2) lie in K₁, so p ≤ Lⁿ(K₁)/(ω_n(r/2)ⁿ). For every y, the sets B̄(x_i,r) ∩ K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y} with y ∈ G(B̄(x_i,r)) cover K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y} and have diameter ≤ 2r, so pre^k_{2r}(K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ S_r(y) := Σ_{i≤p} (2r)^k 1_{G(B̄(x_i,r))}(y) (Mathlib normalization of hausdorffMeasure_apply; S_r is Borel since G(B̄(x_i,r)) is compact), and ∫ S_r dLᵐ ≤ p(2r)^k 2ᵐω(r)(L_G + ω(r))^{m−1}rᵐ ≤ Lⁿ(K₁) 2^{n+k+m} ω(r)(L_G + ω(r))^{m−1}/ω_n → 0 as r → 0 (n = m + k). For fixed δ > 0 and r ≤ δ/2, pre^k_δ ≤ pre^k_{2r} ≤ S_r; along r_j → 0, Fatou gives ∫ liminf_j S_{r_j} = 0, so pre^k_δ(K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for a.e. y; taking δ = 1/l, l ∈ ℕ, μH[k](K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = sup_l pre^k_{1/l}(K′ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for a.e. y, and μHE[k] is a constant multiple of μH[k].
1.2 Transfer to M. Let ψ : V → W ∩ M be a local representation (C¹) and G := f∘ψ (C¹ on V since ψ(V) ⊆ M ⊆ U). Since Dψ(x) maps ℝⁿ isomorphically onto T_{ψ(x)}M (0.1), rank DG(x) = rank L_{ψ(x)}, so by 0.2(a) ψ(C_G) = C ∩ ψ(V). For a compact exhaustion Q_1 ⊆ Q_2 ⊆ … of V, ψ is Lipschitz on each Q_j (C¹), so μHE[k](ψ(Q_j) ∩ C ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = μHE[k](ψ(Q_j ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y})) ≤ Lip(ψ|Q_j)^k μHE[k](Q_j ∩ C_G ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for a.e. y (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). Countably many representations cover M (Lindelöf) and C ⊆ ∪ of countably many ψ_i(Q_{i,j}); hence μHE[k](C ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y.

Step 2 (straightening charts on R). Claim: every x₀ ∈ R has a neighbourhood O ∩ M ⊆ R (O open) parametrized by Ψ : Ω → ℝᴺ, Ω ⊆ ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ open, such that Ψ is C¹, injective, DΨ(ω) injective, Ψ(Ω) = O ∩ M, f(Ψ(a,b)) = a for (a,b) ∈ Ω, and Ψ (transported to ℝⁿ by the linear isometry ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ ≅ ℝⁿ, Euclidean product norm) is a Simon local representation of M on (Ω, O).
Construction. Take a representation ψ : V → W ∩ M with x₀ = ψ(x₀′), G := f∘ψ. DG(x₀′) = L_{x₀}∘Dψ(x₀′) is surjective (J*f(x₀) > 0, 0.2(a), 0.1). Let K₀ := ker DG(x₀′) (dim k), ι : ℝᵏ → K₀ a linear isometry, π_{K₀} the orthogonal projection, and Φ(x) := (G(x), ι⁻¹π_{K₀}(x − x₀′)). DΦ(x₀′) is invertible, so by the C¹ inverse function theorem there is an open V₁ ∋ x₀′, V₁ ⊆ V, such that Φ : V₁ → Ω := Φ(V₁) is a C¹ diffeomorphism onto an open set, with inverse Λ; shrinking V₁ we may assume J*f > 0 on ψ(V₁) (continuity, 0.1). Put Ψ := ψ∘Λ. By 4.2 (SimonGMT exists_open_image_eq_inter) ψ(V₁) = O ∩ M for an open O ⊆ W. Then Ψ is C¹ and injective, DΨ = Dψ(Λ)DΛ is injective, Ψ(Ω) = O ∩ M ⊆ R, f(Ψ(a,b)) = G(Λ(a,b)) = a. Properness: for compact Q ⊆ O, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact and contained in V₁ (ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹Q) ⊆ O ∩ M = ψ(V₁), injectivity), so Ω ∩ Ψ⁻¹(Q) = Φ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q)) is compact.

Step 3 (coarea on one straightening chart). For Ψ, Ω as in Step 2, every Borel E ⊆ Ψ(Ω) and every Borel g : ℝᴺ → [0,∞]: y ↦ ∫_{E∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ is Borel and ∫_E g J*f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{E∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dLᵐ(y).
3.1 E′ := Ψ⁻¹(E) ∩ Ω is Borel. By the weighted area formula for the representation Ψ (SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.weighted_area_formula, or the sibling AreaFormula; Lⁿ on ℝⁿ corresponds to Lᵐ ⊗ Lᵏ under the isometry), ∫_E g J*f dHⁿ = ∫_{E′} g(Ψ) (J*f∘Ψ) JΨ d(a,b), JΨ := √det(DΨ*DΨ).
3.2 For fixed a, Ω_a := {b : (a,b) ∈ Ω} is open and Ψ_a := Ψ(a,·) is C¹, injective, with injective derivative D_bΨ(a,b) = DΨ(a,b)(0,·). Moreover Ψ_a(E′_a) = E ∩ f⁻¹{a}, E′_a := {b : (a,b) ∈ E′}: ⊆ since f∘Ψ(a,b) = a; ⊇ since p ∈ E ∩ f⁻¹{a} is p = Ψ(a′,b) with (a′,b) ∈ E′ and a′ = f(p) = a. The k-dimensional weighted area formula for Ψ_a (injective, injective derivative; SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative) gives ∫_{E∩f⁻¹{a}} g dHᵏ = ∫_{E′_a} g(Ψ(a,b)) J_bΨ(a,b) db, J_bΨ := √det(D_bΨ*D_bΨ).
3.3 Pointwise identity: for (a,b) ∈ Ω, with x = Ψ(a,b), T = T_xM = range DΨ(a,b) (submanifold_tangent applied to the representation Ψ), L = L_x and Θ := DΨ(a,b) regarded as an isomorphism ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ → T: L∘Θ = D(f∘Ψ)(a,b) = (a′,b′) ↦ a′, so Lemma L gives J*f(Ψ(a,b))·JΨ(a,b) = J_bΨ(a,b).
3.4 By Tonelli on ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ, ∫_{E′} g(Ψ)(J*f∘Ψ)JΨ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} (∫_{E′_a} g(Ψ(a,b))J_bΨ(a,b) db) da, the inner integral being a Borel function of a; by 3.2 it equals ∫_{E∩f⁻¹{a}} g dHᵏ. With 3.1 this proves Step 3.

Step 4 (Borel g). Choose straightening charts Ψ_i (i ∈ ℕ) whose images cover R (Lindelöf; Step 2) and put E_i := Ψ_i(Ω_i)∖∪_{l<i}Ψ_l(Ω_l): disjoint Borel sets with union R. For Borel g ≥ 0, by Step 3 and monotone convergence, ∫_R g J*f dHⁿ = Σ_i ∫_{E_i} g J*f dHⁿ = Σ_i ∫ ∫_{E_i∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dy = ∫ ∫_{R∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dy, and y ↦ ∫_{R∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ is Borel. subproblem.title: First variation formula (Simon 2.5.3) and second variation formula (Simon 2.5.4, C³ correction)
subproblem.statement: Let M be an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold of ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U open with U ∩ M ≠ ∅ and Hⁿ(K′ ∩ M) < ∞ for compact K′ ⊆ U, and φ an admissible deformation (IsAdmissibleDeformation r U K φ) with initial velocity X and acceleration Z. (5.3) If r = 2, t ↦ Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) has derivative ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ at t = 0. (5.4) If r = 3, this function is differentiable near 0 and its derivative has derivative ∫_M (div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X)(τ_j·D_{τ_i}X)) dHⁿ at 0.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §5, 5.1-5.4 with the printed derivation (pp. 61-63), and §4 (4.11 chain rule for Jacobians). Erratum applied (GMT/Ch02/README.md): for the second variation 5.4 the deformation is assumed of class C³ instead of C² (with C² the acceleration Z is only continuous, div_M Z is undefined, and the expansion 5.2 to O(t³) needs a third derivative). Depends on the sibling children area_formula (area formula 3.4/3.5; the chart versions in SimonGMT WeightedArea.lean may be used equivalently) and submanifold_tangent (T_yM = range Dψ, M Borel, y ↦ P_y continuous on M).

Setting and notation (frozen definitions). n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). M ⊆ ℝᴺ is an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open, U ∩ M ≠ ∅, μHE[n](K′ ∩ M) < ∞ for every compact K′ ⊆ U, and φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ satisfies IsAdmissibleDeformation r U K φ (r = 2 for FirstVariation, r = 3 for SecondVariation): U open, K ⊆ U compact, Φ(t,x) := φ t x is C^r on (−1,1) × U, φ_0 = id on U, φ_t(x) = x for t ∈ (−1,1) and x ∉ K, and for t ∈ (−1,1) φ_t maps U bijectively onto U with fderiv ℝ φ_t x bijective for x ∈ U. X := initialVelocity φ, X(x) = ∂_tΦ(0,x); Z := initialAcceleration φ, Z(x) = ∂²_tΦ(0,x). For y ∈ M: T_y := tangentSpace M y, P_y := tangentProjection M y, τ_i = τ_i(y) := tangentFrame M y (an orthonormal basis of T_y). Hⁿ := μHE[n]. A(t) := deformedArea n M K φ t = (Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K))).toReal. div_M Y(y) := tangentialDivergence M Y y = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩.

PART I. PRINTED DERIVATION (cleaned transcription).
Let X, Z denote the initial velocity and acceleration of φ_t; then (5.2) φ_t(x) = x + tX_x + (t²/2)Z_x + O(t³), and X, Z have compact support in U. Let M_t = φ_t(M ∩ K). The area formula gives Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ, ψ_t = φ_t|M ∩ U, and hence to compute the first and second variation we can differentiate under the integral; the computation reduces to ∂J_t/∂t and ∂²J_t/∂t² at t = 0. For fixed x, dψ_t|_x(τ) = D_τψ_t = τ + tD_τX + (t²/2)D_τZ + O(t³) (τ ∈ T_xM). Relative to orthonormal bases τ_1,…,τ_n of T_xM and e_1,…,e_{n+ℓ}, dψ_t|_x has i-th row D_{τ_i}ψ_t(x) = τ_i + tD_{τ_i}X + (t²/2)D_{τ_i}Z + O(t³), and (dψ_t|_x)*∘dψ_t|_x has matrix b_ij = δ_ij + t(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X + τ_j·D_{τ_i}X) + t²(½(τ_i·D_{τ_j}Z + τ_j·D_{τ_i}Z) + D_{τ_i}X·D_{τ_j}X) + O(t³). Using det(I + A) = 1 + trace A + ½(trace A)² − ½ trace(A²) + O(|A|³) and √(1+x) = 1 + x/2 − x²/8 + O(x³) one gets J_t = 1 + t div_M X + (t²/2)(div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X)(τ_j·D_{τ_i}X)) + O(t³), where (D_{τ_i}X)^⊥ is the normal part. Thus the area formula yields (5.3) d/dt Hⁿ(M_t)|_{t=0} = ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ and (5.4) d²/dt² Hⁿ(M_t)|_{t=0} = ∫_M (div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X)(τ_j·D_{τ_i}X)) dHⁿ.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF FirstVariation ∧ SecondVariation.

Step 1 (regularity of the deformation).
1. X is C^{r−1} on ℝᴺ and vanishes on ℝᴺ∖K: on U, X = ∂_tΦ(0,·) is C^{r−1}; on the open set ℝᴺ∖K, Φ(t,x) = x for all t ∈ (−1,1), so X = 0 there; the two open sets cover ℝᴺ (K ⊆ U). For r = 3 likewise Z is C¹ on ℝᴺ and Z = 0 off K. In particular X, DX (and Z, DZ) vanish at every point of ℝᴺ∖K.
2. A_t(x) := D_xΦ(t,x) = fderiv ℝ φ_t x is C^{r−1} in (t,x) on (−1,1) × U, and by symmetry of mixed partial derivatives (Φ ∈ C²) ∂_tA_t(x) = D_x∂_tΦ(t,x), so ∂_tA_t(x)|_{t=0} = DX(x); for r = 3 also ∂²_tA_t(x)|_{t=0} = DZ(x). A_0(x) = I for x ∈ U.
3. For t ∈ (−1,1), φ_t is injective on ℝᴺ (on U by BijOn; φ_t maps U into U and fixes ℝᴺ∖U pointwise since ℝᴺ∖U ⊆ ℝᴺ∖K), A_t(x) is invertible for x ∈ U, and φ_t is C¹ on a neighbourhood of K. On the compact set I₀ × K, I₀ := [−½, ½], the continuous functions (t,x) ↦ A_t(x), ∂_tA_t(x) (and ∂²_tA_t(x) for r = 3) are bounded and uniformly continuous, and the smallest singular value of A_t(x) is bounded below by some s₀ > 0.

Step 2 (area formula for M_t). For y ∈ M ∩ K and t ∈ (−1,1) let L_{t,y} := A_t(y)|_{T_y} : T_y → ℝᴺ and J_t(y) := normDet(L_{t,y}) = √det(L_{t,y}*L_{t,y}); in the orthonormal basis τ_i of T_y, J_t(y)² = det b(t,y), b_ij(t,y) := ⟨A_t(y)τ_i, A_t(y)τ_j⟩ (Gram matrix). Claim: for t ∈ (−1,1), Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ < ∞, hence A(t) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ.
4. Choose countably many local representations ψ_i : V_i → W_i ∩ M of M (C¹) whose targets W_i cover M (Lindelöf). Put B_i := (M ∩ K ∩ W_i)∖∪_{l<i}W_l (Borel, as M is Borel by submanifold_tangent), pairwise disjoint with union M ∩ K, and B′_i := V_i ∩ ψ_i⁻¹(B_i) (Borel), so ψ_i(B′_i) = B_i.
5. For x ∈ B′_i, ψ_i(x) ∈ K ⊆ U, so φ_t∘ψ_i is differentiable at x with D(φ_t∘ψ_i)(x) = A_t(ψ_i(x))∘Dψ_i(x), which is injective; and φ_t∘ψ_i is injective on B′_i. By the area formula for injective maps with injective derivative (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_areaJacobianAt, or the sibling AreaFormula applied on compact pieces where the map is Lipschitz), Hⁿ(φ_t(B_i)) = ∫_{B′_i} J(φ_t∘ψ_i) dLⁿ.
6. Chain rule for Jacobians (4.11): for linear L : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ injective and A : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ, normDet(A∘L) = normDet(L)·normDet(A|_{range L}) (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp; SimonGMT areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential). With L = Dψ_i(x), range L = T_{ψ_i(x)} (submanifold_tangent), so J(φ_t∘ψ_i)(x) = Jψ_i(x)·J_t(ψ_i(x)).
7. By the weighted area formula for the representation ψ_i (SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.weighted_area_formula), ∫_{B′_i} Jψ_i·(J_t∘ψ_i) dLⁿ = ∫_{B_i} J_t dHⁿ. Hence Hⁿ(φ_t(B_i)) = ∫_{B_i} J_t dHⁿ. The sets φ_t(B_i) are pairwise disjoint (φ_t injective) and measurable (images of Borel sets under continuous injective maps on Borel sets, e.g. via ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding as in the library), so summing over i gives the claim. Finiteness: for fixed t ∈ (−1,1), J_t(y) ≤ ‖A_t(y)‖ⁿ ≤ sup_{x∈K}‖A_t(x)‖ⁿ < ∞ (A_t is continuous on the compact K) and Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ (hypothesis with K′ = K).
8. Basis-free form and measurability: for y ∈ M, J_t(y) = √det(P_y A_t(y)* A_t(y) P_y + (I − P_y)) (determinant on ℝᴺ; block-diagonal with respect to T_y ⊕ T_y^⊥). Since y ↦ P_y is continuous on M (submanifold_tangent) and A_t is continuous, y ↦ J_t(y) and its t-derivatives below are continuous on M ∩ K, hence Hⁿ⌊M-measurable.

Step 3 (pointwise expansion; the printed computation). Fix y ∈ M ∩ K and write A_t = A_t(y), b(t) = b(t,y). b(0) = I and, by Step 1.2,
 ḃ_ij(0) = ⟨DXτ_i, τ_j⟩ + ⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩, and for r = 3: b̈_ij(0) = ⟨DZτ_i, τ_j⟩ + ⟨τ_i, DZτ_j⟩ + 2⟨DXτ_i, DXτ_j⟩ (DX = DX(y), DZ = DZ(y)).
9. det b(t) = J_t² > 0 for t ∈ (−1,1) (A_t invertible). Jacobi's formula: (det b)′ = det b·tr(b⁻¹ḃ), so (det b)′(0) = tr ḃ(0) = 2Σ_i⟨τ_i, DXτ_i⟩ = 2 div_M X(y). Hence ∂_tJ_t(y)|_{t=0} = (det b)′(0)/(2√det b(0)) = div_M X(y).
10. (r = 3) Differentiating Jacobi's formula once more at 0 (b(0) = I): (det b)″(0) = tr b̈(0) + (tr ḃ(0))² − tr(ḃ(0)²). Then ∂²_tJ_t|_{t=0} = ½(det b)″(0) − ¼((det b)′(0))² = ½tr b̈(0) + ¼(tr ḃ(0))² − ½tr(ḃ(0)²). With a_ij := ⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩: tr b̈(0) = 2div_M Z + 2Σ_i|DXτ_i|², (tr ḃ(0))² = 4(div_M X)², tr(ḃ(0)²) = Σ_{i,j}(a_ij + a_ji)² = 2Σa_ij² + 2Σa_ij a_ji. So ∂²_tJ_t|₀ = div_M Z + (div_M X)² + (Σ_i|DXτ_i|² − Σ_{i,j}a_ji²) − Σ_{i,j}a_ij a_ji, and by Pythagoras |DXτ_i|² = |P_y DXτ_i|² + |(DXτ_i)^⊥|² with |P_yDXτ_i|² = Σ_j⟨τ_j, DXτ_i⟩² = Σ_j a_ji², the bracket equals Σ_i|(DXτ_i)^⊥|², where (v)^⊥ = normalPart M y v = v − P_y v. Since a_ij a_ji = ⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩⟨τ_j, DXτ_i⟩, ∂²_tJ_t(y)|_{t=0} = secondVariationIntegrand M φ y exactly (div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i‖normalPart M y (DX τ_i)‖² − Σ_iΣ_j⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩⟨τ_j, DXτ_i⟩).
11. For y ∈ M∖K both integrands of the frozen statement vanish (X, Z, DX, DZ vanish at y by Step 1.1), consistent with ∫_M = ∫_{M∩K}.

Step 4 (differentiation under the integral sign).
12. Uniform bounds: on I₀ × (M ∩ K), det b(t,y) ≥ s₀^{2n} > 0, and b, ∂_tb (and ∂²_tb for r = 3) are bounded and continuous in t uniformly in y (they are polynomial in A_t(y), ∂_tA_t(y), ∂²_tA_t(y) and the unit vectors τ_i(y), and these are uniformly continuous on I₀ × K by Step 1.3). Hence ∂_tJ_t(y) = ∂_t det b/(2√det b) (and ∂²_tJ_t) are bounded on I₀ × (M ∩ K) by a constant and continuous in t uniformly in y.
13. First variation (r = 2): since Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞, constants are integrable on M ∩ K, and Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le gives that A is differentiable at 0 with A′(0) = ∫_{M∩K} ∂_tJ_t|₀ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩K} div_M X dHⁿ = ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ (Step 3.9 and 3.11; integrability: bounded measurable integrand on a finite-measure set, zero off M ∩ K). This is HasDerivAt (deformedArea n M K φ) (∫ y in M, tangentialDivergence M (initialVelocity φ) y ∂μHE[n]) 0, i.e. FirstVariation.
14. Second variation (r = 3): the same theorem applied at every t₀ ∈ (−½, ½) shows that A is differentiable on (−½, ½) with A′(t) = ∫_{M∩K} ∂_tJ_t dHⁿ, so ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, DifferentiableAt ℝ A t and deriv A = A′ on (−½,½). Applying it once more to t ↦ ∫_{M∩K} ∂_tJ_t dHⁿ (domination of ∂²_tJ_t by a constant) gives HasDerivAt (deriv A) (∫_{M∩K} ∂²_tJ_t|₀ dHⁿ) 0, and by Step 3.10-3.11 the value is ∫_M secondVariationIntegrand M φ y dHⁿ. Since deriv A agrees with A′ on a neighbourhood of 0, HasDerivAt (deriv (deformedArea n M K φ)) (∫ y in M, secondVariationIntegrand M φ y ∂μHE[n]) 0. This is SecondVariation.
15. Remarks: the frame τ(y) may be chosen non-continuously; only the basis-independent quantities J_t(y), div_M X(y) = trace(P_y DX(y)), Σ_i|DXτ_i|² = trace(P_y DX(y)* DX(y) P_y), Σ_{i,j}a_ij a_ji = trace((P_y DX(y) P_y)²) and Σ_i|(DXτ_i)^⊥|² = trace(P_y DX(y)*(I − P_y)DX(y)P_y) enter, and these are continuous on M (Step 2.8), which gives the measurability needed in 13-14. The hypothesis (U ∩ M) ≠ ∅ is not used.

subproblem.title: C¹ Sard-type theorem (Simon 2.6.4)
subproblem.statement: Under the hypotheses of the co-area formula (k ≥ 1, n = m + k, M an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ, f C¹ on an open U ⊇ M), with Z = {x : coareaJacobian M f x = 0}: (1) {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0} = {x ∈ M : rank of Df(x) restricted to T_xM < m}; (2) Hᵏ(M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y; (3) for every y, M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z = M ∩ F for some closed F, and (M ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ∖ Z is a k-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §6, the paragraph after 6.3 and Theorem 6.4 (p. 66-67). Readings applied (GMT/Ch02/README.md): the printed identity C = {x ∈ M : rank df_x < m} is included as a conjunct; (closed set) is read as relatively closed in M (M need not be closed in ℝᴺ); the empty set is (vacuously) a submanifold. Depends on the siblings coarea_formula (CoareaFormula) and submanifold_tangent (T_xM = range Dψ, M Borel, x ↦ P_x continuous on M).

Statement (frozen C1Sard). N, m, k ∈ ℕ, k ≥ 1, n := m + k, M ⊆ ℝᴺ an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open with M ⊆ U, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ on U. With J*f(x) := coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L_xL_x*), L_x := Df(x)∘ι_{T_xM} : T_xM → ℝᵐ (ι the inclusion), and Z := {x : J*f(x) = 0}: (1) {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0} = {x ∈ M : finrank(range L_x) < m}; (2) for Lᵐ-a.e. y, Hᵏ(M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z) = 0 (Hᵏ = μHE[k]); (3) for every y ∈ ℝᵐ there is a closed F ⊆ ℝᴺ with M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z = M ∩ F, and (M ∩ f⁻¹{y})∖Z is a k-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ.

PART I. PRINTED ARGUMENT (cleaned transcription).
An important consequence of 6.3 is that if C = {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0}, then (by using 6.3 with A = C) Hᵏ(C ∩ f⁻¹(y)) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ. Also, since J*f(x) ≠ 0 precisely when df_x has rank m, the implicit function theorem implies that either f⁻¹(y)∖C is empty or else it is a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold in the sense of §4. Theorem 6.4 (C¹ Sard-type theorem): for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ f(M), f⁻¹(y) decomposes into a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold and a closed set of Hᵏ-measure zero: f⁻¹(y) = (f⁻¹(y)∖C) ∪ (f⁻¹(y) ∩ C), C = {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0} (= {x ∈ M : rank df_x < m}), Hᵏ(f⁻¹(y) ∩ C) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y, and f⁻¹(y)∖C is either empty or a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF.

Conjunct (1) (linear algebra; valid for every x).
1. Let L := L_x : T → ℝᵐ, T := T_xM with the induced inner product. LL* is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite (⟨LL*w, w⟩ = |L*w|²), so det(LL*) ≥ 0 and J*f(x) = √det(LL*) = 0 ⟺ det(LL*) = 0 (Real.sqrt d = 0 ⟺ d ≤ 0).
2. det(LL*) = 0 ⟺ LL* is not injective ⟺ ∃ w ≠ 0 with L*w = 0 (if LL*w = 0 then |L*w|² = ⟨LL*w, w⟩ = 0) ⟺ L* is not injective ⟺ L is not surjective (range L = (ker L*)^⊥) ⟺ finrank(range L) < m. Here range L = LinearMap.range ((fderiv ℝ f x).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (tangentSpace M x).subtype). Intersecting with M gives (1).

Conjunct (2) (from the coarea formula).
3. C_M := {x ∈ M : J*f(x) = 0} = M ∩ Z is a Borel set: by submanifold_tangent M is Borel and x ↦ P_x is continuous on M, and for x ∈ M, L_xL_x* = Df(x)P_xDf(x)* (ι ι* = P_x) with Df continuous on U ⊇ M, so J*f is continuous on M and C_M is relatively closed in M.
4. Apply CoareaFormula with g := indicator of C_M (Borel, hence AEMeasurable for μHE[m+k] restricted to M). Left side: ∫_M 1_{C_M} J*f dHⁿ = 0 since J*f = 0 on C_M. Right side: for each y, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{y}} 1_{C_M} dHᵏ = Hᵏ((M ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ∩ C_M) = Hᵏ(M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z) (C_M measurable). Hence ∫ Hᵏ(M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z) dLᵐ(y) = 0, and the integrand is AEMeasurable (first conclusion of CoareaFormula), so it vanishes for Lᵐ-a.e. y (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff′). This is (2).

Conjunct (3a) (relative closedness).
5. Fix y. S_y := M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ∩ Z is relatively closed in M: if x_j ∈ S_y and x_j → x ∈ M, then f(x) = y (f continuous at x ∈ U) and J*f(x) = lim J*f(x_j) = 0 (continuity of J*f on M, step 3). Put F := closure S_y (closed); then M ∩ F = S_y (⊇ trivial; ⊆ by relative closedness).

Conjunct (3b) (the regular part of a fiber is a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold).
6. Let Σ_y := (M ∩ f⁻¹{y})∖Z. Since r = 1 ≥ 1 it suffices, for each p ∈ Σ_y, to produce an open D ⊆ ℝᵏ, an open W₃ ⊆ ℝᴺ with p ∈ W₃ and χ : ℝᵏ → ℝᴺ such that IsSimonLocalRepresentation 1 Σ_y D W₃ χ: χ C¹ on D, injective on D, χ(D) = W₃ ∩ Σ_y, proper relative to (D, W₃), Dχ(z) injective for z ∈ D. (If Σ_y = ∅ there is nothing to prove.)
7. Construction. Take a C¹ local representation ψ : V → W ∩ M with p ∈ W, x_p := ψ⁻¹(p), and G := f∘ψ (C¹ on V since ψ(V) ⊆ M ⊆ U). By submanifold_tangent Dψ(x_p) maps ℝⁿ onto T_pM, and L_p is surjective by steps 1-2 because J*f(p) ≠ 0 (p ∉ Z), so DG(x_p) = L_p∘Dψ(x_p) is surjective. Let K_p := ker DG(x_p) (dimension k), ι : ℝᵏ → K_p a linear isometry, π_{K_p} the orthogonal projection, and Φ(x) := (G(x), ι⁻¹π_{K_p}(x − x_p)) ∈ ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ; note Φ(x_p) = (f(p), 0) = (y, 0). DΦ(x_p) is injective (if DG(x_p)ζ = 0 and π_{K_p}ζ = 0 then ζ ∈ K_p ∩ K_p^⊥ = 0), hence invertible. By the C¹ inverse function theorem there are an open V₁ ∋ x_p, V₁ ⊆ V, and an open Ω₁ ∋ (y,0) with Φ : V₁ → Ω₁ a C¹ diffeomorphism; Λ := (Φ|V₁)⁻¹ is C¹. Shrink V₁ so that J*f > 0 on ψ(V₁) (continuity of J*f∘ψ at x_p) and choose ρ > 0 with B(y,ρ) × B(0,ρ) ⊆ Ω₁. Put D := B(0,ρ) ⊆ ℝᵏ, χ(z) := ψ(Λ(y,z)), V₃ := Λ(B(y,ρ) × B(0,ρ)) (open, ⊆ V₁), and by 4.2 (SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.exists_open_image_eq_inter) an open W₃ ⊆ W with ψ(V₃) = W₃ ∩ M. Then p = χ(0) ∈ W₃ (Λ(y,0) = x_p).
8. χ(D) = W₃ ∩ Σ_y. (⊆) For z ∈ D, x := Λ(y,z) ∈ V₃, χ(z) = ψ(x) ∈ W₃ ∩ M, f(χ(z)) = G(x) = (Φ(x))₁ = y, and J*f(χ(z)) > 0 since x ∈ V₁; so χ(z) ∈ Σ_y. (⊇) If q ∈ W₃ ∩ Σ_y then q ∈ W₃ ∩ M = ψ(V₃), q = ψ(x) with x ∈ V₃, Φ(x) = (a, z′) ∈ B(y,ρ) × B(0,ρ) and a = G(x) = f(q) = y, so x = Λ(y,z′) and q = χ(z′) with z′ ∈ D.
9. Regularity. χ is C¹ on D; injective (Λ(y,·) and ψ injective); Dχ(z) = Dψ(Λ(y,z))∘DΛ(y,z)(0,·) is injective (DΛ invertible, Dψ injective).
10. Properness relative to (D, W₃). Let Q ⊆ W₃ be compact. V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact (properness of ψ; Q ⊆ W) and contained in V₃ (ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹Q) ⊆ Q ∩ M ⊆ W₃ ∩ M = ψ(V₃), injectivity). Hence Φ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q)) is a compact subset of B(y,ρ) × B(0,ρ), and D ∩ χ⁻¹(Q) = {z : (y,z) ∈ Φ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q))} is compact (a closed slice of a compact set, contained in D).
11. Steps 7-10 show that (D, W₃, χ) is a C¹ Simon local representation of Σ_y around p with parameter space ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); as p ∈ Σ_y was arbitrary, IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝᵏ) 1 Σ_y. (When m = 0 the same construction applies, with Φ = ι⁻¹π_{K_p}(· − x_p) and K_p = ℝⁿ.) Steps 1-11 prove C1Sard.

J*f continuous on M (continuity of P), so C_M = M ∩ Z is Borel and relatively closed in M.
Co-area formula with g = 1_{C_M}: ∫ Hᵏ(M ∩ f⁻¹y ∩ Z) dy = ∫_{C_M} J*f = 0, hence a.e. zero.
Relative closedness by continuity of f and J*f; F = closure.
Regular fibers: chart ψ, G = f∘ψ submersion at the point, inverse function theorem for (G, projection to ker DG), slice chart χ(z) = ψ(Λ(y,z)) is a proper injective C¹ immersion onto W₃ ∩ fiber.

subproblem.title: Stationary iff mean curvature vanishes (Simon 2.5.5(2)) and second variation of stationary submanifolds (Simon 2.5.11, C³ correction)
subproblem.statement: (5.5(2)) If M is an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold of ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U is open and closure U ∩ M is compact, then M is stationary in U (IsStationaryIn) iff the mean curvature meanCurvature M y = 0 for all y ∈ M ∩ U. (5.11) If M is a C² Simon submanifold, U open with (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅, M stationary in U, and φ an admissible C³ deformation whose initial velocity X is normal to M along M, then t ↦ Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) is differentiable near 0 and its derivative has derivative ∫_M (Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(X·B(τ_i,τ_j))²) dHⁿ at 0.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2: §4 (4.21-4.30: divergence theorem, second fundamental form, mean curvature, div_M X^⊥ = −X·H) and §5 (Lemma 5.5(2) and Lemma 5.11 with their printed proofs), pp. 59-65. Errata/readings applied (GMT/Ch02/README.md): in 5.11 the deformation is C³ instead of C²; stationarity is the variational definition IsStationaryIn (finiteness of Hⁿ(M ∩ K) for compact K ⊆ U, and zero first variation for every admissible C² deformation), so the identities used in the printed proofs are derived from it; B is the frame-free form B_y(τ,η) = (D_τP)η (equal to Simon's 4.24, see the contract docstring). The book states the divergence theorem 4.21/4.22(*) without proof; a complete proof of the compact-support version is given in Part II.1. Depends on the siblings variation_formulas (FirstVariation, SecondVariation), area_formula (area formula) and submanifold_tangent (T_yM = range Dψ, M Borel, P continuous on M).

Notation. N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For y ∈ M: T_y = tangentSpace M y, P_y = tangentProjection M y, τ_i = tangentFrame M y, B_y(τ,η) := secondFundamentalForm M y τ η = fderivWithin ℝ P M y τ η, H(y) := meanCurvature M y = Σ_i B_y(τ_i,τ_i), div_M Y(y) := Σ_i⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩ (= trace(P_y DY(y)), basis independent).

PART I. PRINTED PROOFS (cleaned transcription).
4.29-4.30: decompose X = X^T + X^⊥ with X^⊥ = Σ_α(ν^α·X)ν^α; then div_M X^⊥ = Σ_α(ν^α·X)div_M ν^α, so by 4.28 div_M X^⊥ = −X·H; on the other hand ∫_M div_M X^T = −∫_{∂M} X·η by 4.21; hence ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ = −∫_M X·H dHⁿ − ∫_{∂M} X·η dH^{n−1}.
Lemma 5.5. Suppose M is a C² submanifold with mean curvature vector H and U open. (2) If Ū ∩ M is a compact subset of M, then M is stationary in U if and only if H ≡ 0 on M ∩ U. (Printed: in view of 4.30, with the remark after 5.4 that by the first variation formula stationarity is equivalent to ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ = 0 for all C¹ X with compact support in U.)
Lemma 5.11. If M is C², stationary in U, U open with (M̄∖M) ∩ U = ∅, and if X as in 5.4 has compact support in U with X_y ∈ (T_yM)^⊥ for y ∈ M, then 5.4 says d²/dt² Hⁿ(M_t)|_{t=0} = ∫_M (Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(X·B(τ_i,τ_j))²) dHⁿ. Printed proof: First ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0 by virtue of the fact that M is stationary in U, and div_M X = −X·H = 0 by virtue of 4.29 and 5.5(2) and the fact that X is normal to M. The proof is then completed by noting that τ_i·D_{τ_j}X = −X·B(τ_i,τ_j) by virtue of 4.24 and the fact that X is normal to M.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF StationaryIffMeanCurvatureZero ∧ SecondVariationStationary.

II.0′ Regularity and support of the initial velocity and acceleration (self-contained; these facts are not part of the exported statements of the siblings). Let φ satisfy IsAdmissibleDeformation r U K φ and Φ(t,x) := φ t x. On U, X = initialVelocity φ = ∂_tΦ(0,·) is C^{r−1} and Z = initialAcceleration φ = ∂²_tΦ(0,·) is C^{r−2} (for x ∈ U and t ∈ (−1,1), deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t = ∂_tΦ(t,x) because Φ is C^r on the open set (−1,1) × U). On the open set ℝᴺ∖K, t ↦ φ t x is constant (= x) on (−1,1), so X = 0 and Z = 0 there. Since K ⊆ U, the open sets U and ℝᴺ∖K cover ℝᴺ; hence X is C^{r−1} and Z is C^{r−2} on ℝᴺ, both vanish on ℝᴺ∖K, and so do their derivatives DX, DZ at every point of ℝᴺ∖K. In particular for r = 2, X is C¹ on ℝᴺ with X = 0 off K; for r = 3, X is C² and Z is C¹ on ℝᴺ, vanishing off K.

II.0 Geometry of a C² Simon submanifold. Let M be an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold of ℝᴺ and ψ : V → W ∩ M a local representation of class ≥ 2 with ψ(x₀) = y₀. Write ∂_kψ, ∂_k∂_lψ for partial derivatives, g_kl := ⟨∂_kψ, ∂_lψ⟩ (C¹, positive definite), (g^{kl}) its inverse, √g := √det(g_kl) = Jψ.
G0 (projection onto the range of an injective map). For an injective linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ, A*A is invertible and Π(A) := A(A*A)⁻¹A* satisfies Π(A)* = Π(A), Π(A)² = Π(A), Π(A)A = A and Π(A)w = 0 for w ⊥ range A (A*w = 0); hence Π(A) is the orthogonal projection onto range A. The set of injective A is open and A ↦ Π(A) is C^∞ there (composition, adjoint and inversion of invertible operators are smooth). Since tangentSpace M ψ(x) = range Dψ(x) (submanifold_tangent), P_{ψ(x)} = Π(Dψ(x)) for x ∈ V.
G1 (P is C¹ along M). By G0, P∘ψ = Π∘Dψ is C¹ on V (Dψ is C¹ because ψ is C²). Choose a linear isomorphism Q₀ : ℝ^ℓ → (range Dψ(x₀))^⊥ and apply the inverse function theorem to Ξ(x,w) := ψ(x) + Q₀w (C², DΞ(x₀,0) invertible): there are open O ∋ y₀ and a C² map π : O → V with π(ψ(x)) = x for x near x₀; shrinking, by 4.2 (SimonGMT exists_open_image_eq_inter) O ∩ M = ψ(V₀) for an open V₀ on which π∘ψ = id. Then P̃ := Π(Dψ(π(·))) is C¹ on O and P̃ = P on O ∩ M. Hence HasFDerivWithinAt P (DP̃(y)) M y for y ∈ O ∩ M, and since any two derivatives within M agree on the tangent cone of M at y, which contains T_y (every v ∈ T_y is γ′(0) for a C¹ curve in M, by submanifold_tangent), B_y(τ,η) = DP̃(y)[τ]η for τ ∈ T_y (independent of the choice made by fderivWithin).
G2 (formula, symmetry, normality). For y = ψ(x), τ = Dψ(x)a, η = Dψ(x)b: differentiating P̃(ψ(x′))Dψ(x′)b = Dψ(x′)b at x′ = x in direction a gives B_y(τ,η) + P_y D²ψ(x)[a,b] = D²ψ(x)[a,b], so B_y(τ,η) = (I − P_y)D²ψ(x)[a,b]: B_y is symmetric on T_y × T_y with values in T_y^⊥. Writing τ_i = Dψ(x)a_i one has Σ_i a_i a_iᵀ = (g_kl)⁻¹, hence H(ψ(x)) = (I − P_{ψ(x)}) Σ_{k,l} g^{kl}(x)∂_k∂_lψ(x); in particular H is continuous on M.
G3 (normal fields). Each DP̃(y)[τ] is self-adjoint (derivative of a self-adjoint-valued map). If Y is C¹ near y ∈ M and P_zY(z) = 0 for all z ∈ M near y, then for τ, η ∈ T_y: ⟨η, DY(y)τ⟩ = −⟨Y(y), B_y(τ,η)⟩. Proof: z ↦ P̃(z)Y(z) is C¹ on O and vanishes on O ∩ M, so its derivative vanishes on T_y (derivative along C¹ curves in M): DP̃(y)[τ]Y(y) + P_y DY(y)τ = 0; pair with η ∈ T_y and use self-adjointness: ⟨η, DY(y)τ⟩ = ⟨η, P_yDY(y)τ⟩ = −⟨DP̃(y)[τ]η, Y(y)⟩.

II.1 Divergence identity (4.22(*) + 4.29 ⇒ 4.30 without boundary). Claim D: let M be a C² Simon submanifold, Y : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ of class C¹ with Y = 0 outside a closed set S such that M ∩ S is compact. Then div_M Y and ⟨Y,H⟩ are bounded, continuous on M, vanish on M∖S, are integrable for Hⁿ⌊M, and ∫_M div_M Y dHⁿ = −∫_M ⟨Y, H⟩ dHⁿ.
